data.title: Representing Python notebooks as dataflow graphs
data.author: akshayka
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种新型的开源Python笔记本工具——marimo，它通过数据流图（dataflow graphs）来解决传统笔记本（如Jupyter）在可重复性、交互性、可维护性和可重用性方面的问题。传统笔记本容易积累隐藏状态，导致代码和输出不同步，影响可重复性。此外，它们的JSON格式使得版本控制和代码重用困难。marimo将笔记本表示为数据流图，集成了反应式计算，能保持代码和输出的同步，并支持将笔记本作为可执行脚本、Python模块和交互式Web应用使用。这种设计提升了AI和数据工作的效率和可靠性。marimo旨在解决传统笔记本的不足，提供更具交互性、可维护性和重用性的解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Marimo及其他笔记本工具的优缺点，以及在数据分析和可重复性方面的应用。

不同观点：
• **支持Marimo**：[data-ottawa] 非常喜欢Marimo，尤其是它的交互式组件和与队友共享笔记本的便捷性。他们提到Marimo在处理图表方面比Jupyter更直观，并且对软件的质量和开发团队的响应速度表示赞赏。
• **对Marimo的期望不同**：[createaccount99] 原本期待的是一个流程编辑器GUI，暗示Marimo的功能与他们的预期不符。
• **笔记本的可重复性**：[getnormality] 认为Jupyter笔记本的可重复性问题并非难以解决，只需在完成后自行验证结果。同时提到大数据和执行混乱可能带来的挑战，并对Marimo表示认可。
• **对“修复笔记本可重复性危机”工具的质疑**：[Galanwe] 认为这些工具仅对有经验的开发者有用，而新手不会去使用增加复杂性的工具。他们认为通过简单的操作如“重启内核并运行所有”可以解决大部分问题。
• **与其他工具的比较**：[nylonstrung] 认为Marimo与Streamlit或Observable类似，适合喜欢这些工具的用户。
• **Marimo的实际体验**：[tastyminerals2] 分享了他们使用Marimo的积极经验，特别是变量去重和逻辑分离方面的好处，认为这有助于编写更结构化的Python代码。
• **对外部系统标记的需求**：[PeterStuer] 提出是否需要对接触外部Python系统的任何内容进行“volatile”标记。
• **对笔记本嵌入数据管道的反对**：[probablypower] 认为将笔记本嵌入数据管道是不好的做法，尽管认可文章的写作质量和阅读价值。

补充讨论：
• **对笔记本执行模型的批评**：[riedel] 指出笔记本的执行模型仍然存在问题，尤其是在处理函数和类的定义时。他们希望看到像编译器中的SSA形式那样的DAG支持，并认为笔记本界面的调整是必要的。
• **对行业交叉创新的看法**：[philsnow] 对外部行业明显的问题（如笔记本中过时的中间结果）在笔记本生态系统中未被解决表示惊讶，认为可能是因为缺乏跨行业的交流。

争议焦点：
• **笔记本工具的复杂性与用户需求**：[Galanwe] 认为复杂的工具对新手不友好，而[getnormality] 则认为通过简单的操作可以解决大部分问题。
• **笔记本在数据管道中的角色**：[probablypower] 反对将笔记本嵌入数据管道，而[data-ottawa] 则赞赏Marimo在团队协作和数据分析中的应用。

总结：讨论围绕Marimo等笔记本工具的优缺点展开，涉及可重复性、复杂性、执行模型等方面，并反映了不同用户对工具功能和应用场景的不同期望与看法。

August 4, 2025
Python notebooks as dataflow graphs: reactive, reproducible, and reusable
Akshay
@
akshaykagrawal
This blog is adapted from our talk at PyCon 2025. marimo is free and open
source, available on
GitHub
. For
a free online experience with link sharing, try
molab
.
marimo is a new kind of open-source Python notebook. While traditional
notebooks are just REPLs, marimo notebooks are Python programs represented as
dataflow graphs. This intermediate representation lets marimo
blend the best parts of interactive computing with the reproducibility and
reusability of Python software: every marimo notebook works as a reactive
notebook for Python (and SQL) that keeps code and outputs in sync (run a cell
and marimo knows which other cells to run), an executable script and a Python
module, and an interactive web app.
In this blog post, we motivate the need for a new kind of notebook, explain how
and why marimo represents notebooks as dataflow graphs, present design
decisions we made to help users adapt to dataflow programming, discuss
our implementation, and show several examples of how marimo uses its dataflow
graph to make data work reactive, interactive, reproducible, and reusable.
Contents.
Motivating a new kind of notebook
marimo: a new kind of notebook
Representation as a dataflow graph
How marimo uses the dataflow graph
Implementation
Conclusion
Motivating a new kind of notebook
AI and data work are different from software engineering.
When you work with data, it’s helpful to hold objects in memory,
iteratively transforming and visualizing them as you evaluate
datasets, models, and algorithms. Notebooks are the only programming
environment that enable this workflow — for this reason, the number of GitHub
repos with Jupyter notebooks
more than doubled in
2024
,
alongside the rise of AI.
Interactive computing is crucial for evaluating
data and algorithms. These GIFs visualize projected LBFGS
applied to different embedding formulations on the MNIST dataset.
I made them in Jupyter notebooks during my PhD in machine learning;
I used Jupyter notebooks extensively during my PhD, but I also had
issues in reproducibility, interactivity, maintainability, and reusability,
which motivated me to start work on marimo.
Nonetheless, traditional notebooks such as Google Colab or Jupyter notebooks
suffer from issues in reproducibility, interactivity, maintainability, and
reusability, making them unsuited for modern AI and data work and creating
the need for a new kind of notebook.
Reproducibility
Traditional notebooks have a reproducibility crisis. In
2019, a
study
from New
York University and Federal Fluminense University found that of the nearly
1 million Jupyter notebooks on GitHub with valid execution orders, only 24%
could be re-run, and just 4% reproduced the same results. A
similar
study
from 2020 by JetBrains found that over a third of the notebooks on GitHub had
invalid execution histories.
Traditional notebooks accumulate hidden state: run or delete a cell,
and program memory is imperatively mutated without regard to the rest of the
code on the page. This allows code and outputs to become out of sync. While a feature of
REPLs, hidden state gets in the way when you’re trying to do work you’d like to
reproduce.
Code and outputs in traditional notebooks
can become out of sync
These studies can be scrutinized and caveated, but the finding resonates with
developer sentiment at large, not to mention my own experience as a former
machine learning PhD student who used notebooks on an almost daily basis.
You
have to be very disciplined
to make a
Jupyter notebook that is actually reproducible. At least for the
kind of work that I do, I’d prefer a tool that was reproducible by default.
Interactivity
While Jupyter notebooks are interactive in that you can execute cells
iteratively,
data
in traditional notebooks is not interactive. As a
researcher, I wanted to make selections in scatter plots and get my selection
back as a dataframe automatically. These kinds of highly interactive
experiences were simply out of reach.
Maintainability
Jupyter’s JSON file format and the fact that
Jupyter notebooks are not well-formed programs makes code reuse difficult.
Because traditional notebooks are not Python files but instead stored with code
and outputs serialized in what
Pydantic creator Samuel Colvin calls a “horrid
blob”
of JSON, they are difficult to
maintain. Instead of reusing code, practitioners end up duplicating notebooks
or starting from scratch. (The file format also makes it hard to version
notebooks with Git.)
Reusability
Finally, because traditional notebooks aren’t guaranteed to be valid Python
programs, they are difficult to reuse as data pipelines, as apps, or software.
And yet people try anyway (just look at Databricks and SageMaker), because
AI and data
people really like interactive programming environments
.

data.title: Long-term exposure to outdoor air pollution linked to increased risk of dementia
data.author: hhs
data.article_summary: 剑桥大学研究发现，长期暴露于户外空气污染，尤其是PM2.5、二氧化氮和煤烟，会增加患痴呆症的风险。研究团队对51项研究进行了系统回顾和荟萃分析，数据涵盖近3000万人，主要来自高收入国家。结果显示，PM2.5每增加10微克/立方米，痴呆症的相对风险就会上升。空气污染已被确定为痴呆症的一个风险因素，控制空气污染有助于带来长期健康、社会、气候和经济效益。全球痴呆症病例预计将从目前的5740万例增加到2050年的1.528亿例，因此减少空气污染对降低痴呆症风险至关重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：空气污染（特别是PM2.5）的组成、健康影响、社会不平等以及应对措施

不同观点：
• PM2.5的组成和影响是复杂且多样的：
  ◦ [ahaucnx] 指出PM2.5只是定义了颗粒的直径，但其成分可能非常不同，包括盐、有毒金属等。目前对其健康影响的理解仍不足，需要更多研究来明确不同来源（如交通、工厂、港口等）的污染对健康的具体影响。

• 空气污染与社会不平等：
  ◦ [cjtrowbridge] 认为空气污染暴露与贫困和边缘化密切相关，指出Alameda县的研究发现，由于空气污染不平等，黑人平均寿命比白人短15年，这是环境正义中的典型问题。

• 城市规划与空气污染暴露：
  ◦ [01100011] 提到在圣地亚哥，很多优质日托中心靠近高速公路，质疑这种规划的合理性，并提到新建的公寓楼靠近高速公路的现象，表达对这种规划的不满。

• 政治因素与空气质量改善的缓慢进展：
  ◦ [KolibriFly] 批评政治进程缓慢，尽管已有数十年的技术知识可以减少交通和能源产生的污染，但实际进展有限。

• 对统计数据的质疑：
  ◦ [unsupp0rted] 质疑全球痴呆症统计数据的有效性，认为应使用百分比或每千人发病率来表达，以便更好地理解问题的严重性。

• 痴呆症与其他因素的潜在关联：
  ◦ [hodgehog11] 提到最近一项研究声称锂耗竭可能与阿尔茨海默病有关，并询问空气污染是否可能通过某种机制影响锂水平。

• 个人应对高污染环境的方法：
  ◦ [8s2ngy] 询问在污染严重的城市中如何最小化空气污染的影响，表达了对个人控制能力的无力感。

补充讨论：
• 对具体应对措施的建议：
  ◦ [alliao] 建议广泛使用空气过滤设备（如CR box），认为在任何花费合理时间的地方都值得安装过滤器，认为这是实际可行的解决方案。

• 对当前政策变化的关注：
  ◦ [joshuamoyers] 提到当前政府削弱清洁空气法的行动，并提供相关新闻链接，表达对政策变化的担忧。

• 个人经验分享：
  ◦ [lemonberry] 作为痴呆症患者的唯一照顾者，分享了照顾父亲的困难经历，呼吁提前规划老年护理，并建议建立支持网络。

• 对城市政策的赞同：
  ◦ [pacifika] 认为ULEZ（超低排放区）政策是正确的决定，支持通过政策限制车辆排放。

争议焦点：
• 对统计数据的理解和表达方式存在争议：
  ◦ [unsupp0rted] 对全球痴呆症病例数的表达方式提出质疑，认为需要更具比较性的数据形式。

• 对空气污染健康影响的机制和具体因素（如锂耗竭）的关联性存在疑问：
  ◦ [hodgehog11] 提出的锂耗竭与空气污染的关系问题，尚未有明确答案或研究支持。

总结：讨论涵盖了PM2.5的复杂性、空气污染对健康和社会不平等的影响、城市规划问题、政治进展缓慢以及个人应对措施等多个方面，展现了对空气污染问题多维度的关注和思考。

Long-term exposure to outdoor air pollution linked to increased risk of dementia
An analysis of studies incorporating data from almost 30 million people has highlighted the role that air pollution – including that coming from car exhaust emissions – plays in increased risk of dementia.
Tackling air pollution can deliver long-term health, social, climate, and economic benefits
Haneen Khreis
Dementias such as Alzheimer's disease are estimated to affect more than 57.4 million people worldwide, a number that is expected to almost triple to 152.8 million cases by 2050. The impacts on the individuals, families and caregivers and society at large are immense.
While there are some indications that the prevalence of dementia is decreasing in Europe and North America, suggesting that it may be possible to reduce the risk of the disease at a population level, elsewhere the picture is less promising.
Air pollution has recently been identified as a risk factor for dementia, with several studies pointing the finger at a number of pollutants. However, the strength of evidence and ability to determine a causal effect has been varied.
In a paper published in The Lancet Planetary Health, a team led by researchers at the Medical Research Council (MRC) Epidemiology Unit, University of Cambridge, carried out a systematic review and meta-analysis of existing scientific literature to examine this link further. This approach allowed them to bring together studies that on their own may not provide sufficient evidence, and which sometimes disagree with each other, to provide more robust overarching conclusions.
In total, the researchers included 51 studies, including data from more than 29 million participants who had been exposed to air pollutants for at least one year, mostly from high-income countries. Of these, 34 papers were included in the meta-analysis: 15 originated in North America, 10 in Europe, seven in Asia, and two in Australia.
The researchers found a positive and statistically-significant association between 3 types of air pollutant and dementia. These were:
Particulate matter with a diameter of 2.5 microns or less (PM
2.5
)
, a pollutant made up of tiny particles small enough that they can be inhaled deep into the lungs. These particles come from several sources, including vehicle emissions, power plants, industrial processes, wood burning stoves and fireplaces, and construction dust. They also form in the atmosphere because of complex chemical reactions involving other pollutants such as sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides. The particles can stay in the air for a long time and travel a long way from where they were produced.
Nitrogen dioxide (NO
2
)
, one of the key pollutants that arise from burning fossil fuels. It is found in vehicle exhaust, especially diesel exhaust, and industrial emissions, as well as those from gas stoves and heaters. Exposure to high concentrations of nitrogen dioxide can irritate the respiratory system, worsening and inducing conditions like asthma and reducing lung function.
Soot
from sources such as vehicle exhaust emissions and burning wood. It can trap heat and affect the climate. When inhaled, it can penetrate deep into the lungs, aggravating respiratory diseases and increasing the risk of heart problems.

• 城市规划与空气污染暴露：
  ◦ [01100011] 提到在圣地亚哥，很多优质日托中心靠近高速公路，质疑这种规划的合理性，并提到新建的公寓楼靠近高速公路的现象，表达对这种规划的不满。

• 政治因素与空气质量改善的缓慢进展：
  ◦ [KolibriFly] 批评政治进程缓慢，尽管已有数十年的技术知识可以减少交通和能源产生的污染，但实际进展有限。

• 对统计数据的质疑：
  ◦ [unsupp0rted] 质疑全球痴呆症统计数据的有效性，认为应使用百分比或每千人发病率来表达，以便更好地理解问题的严重性。

• 痴呆症与其他因素的潜在关联：
  ◦ [hodgehog11] 提到最近一项研究声称锂耗竭可能与阿尔茨海默病有关，并询问空气污染是否可能通过某种机制影响锂水平。

• 个人应对高污染环境的方法：
  ◦ [8s2ngy] 询问在污染严重的城市中如何最小化空气污染的影响，表达了对个人控制能力的无力感。

补充讨论：
• 对具体应对措施的建议：
  ◦ [alliao] 建议广泛使用空气过滤设备（如CR box），认为在任何花费合理时间的地方都值得安装过滤器，认为这是实际可行的解决方案。

• 对当前政策变化的关注：
  ◦ [joshuamoyers] 提到当前政府削弱清洁空气法的行动，并提供相关新闻链接，表达对政策变化的担忧。

• 个人经验分享：
  ◦ [lemonberry] 作为痴呆症患者的唯一照顾者，分享了照顾父亲的困难经历，呼吁提前规划老年护理，并建议建立支持网络。

• 对城市政策的赞同：
  ◦ [pacifika] 认为ULEZ（超低排放区）政策是正确的决定，支持通过政策限制车辆排放。

争议焦点：
• 对统计数据的理解和表达方式存在争议：
  ◦ [unsupp0rted] 对全球痴呆症病例数的表达方式提出质疑，认为需要更具比较性的数据形式。

• 对空气污染健康影响的机制和具体因素（如锂耗竭）的关联性存在疑问：
  ◦ [hodgehog11] 提出的锂耗竭与空气污染的关系问题，尚未有明确答案或研究支持。

总结：讨论涵盖了PM2.5的复杂性、空气污染对健康和社会不平等的影响、城市规划问题、政治进展缓慢以及个人应对措施等多个方面，展现了对空气污染问题多维度的关注和思考。

data.title: Quickshell – building blocks for your desktop
data.author: abhinavk
data.article_summary: Quickshell 0.2.0版本发布，这是一个基于QtQuick的工具包，用于构建状态栏、小部件、锁屏等桌面组件。它支持与Wayland合成器或窗口管理器配合使用，创建完整的桌面环境。主要特点包括：实时加载配置更改、使用简单直观的QML语言（支持LSP）、提供丰富集成功能，并展示了通过QML代码创建变色窗口的示例。项目提供安装指南和文档支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Quickshell及其相关技术（如QML、i3wm、Qt等）在GUI开发中的应用与发展

不同观点：
• [vhantz] 认为QML是近期GUI开发中最出色的工具之一，但其使用率不足。他分享了自己类似的项目（qi3pc和buffalo），并指出这些项目还未达到1.0版本，文档也较少。他专注于X11/i3wm，并通过自己的项目将i3的IPC机制与Qt的信号/槽机制结合。

• [conradev] 提到利用GitHub搜索查看其他人如何使用Quickshell，并表示对该项目的赞赏。

• [riidom] 关注更新订阅问题，指出Forgejo RSS中缺少仅限发布的feed，并提供了一个GitHub镜像链接以便订阅发布。

• [gr4vityWall] 认为Quickshell在迭代速度上比其他原生/非基于Web的工具包有显著改进，但希望有除了QML之外的其他脚本选项，并希望能利用React生态系统。

• [nylonstrung] 推荐了另一个使用Quickshell和Niri合成器的项目（DankMaterialShell），并提供了链接。

• [0x696C6961] 强烈认为QML未得到足够重视。

• [jp1016] 赞赏模块化“构建块”的理念，并提到自己正在开发类似的项目（BeaverGrow），用于构建自定义仪表板，并提供了链接。

• [nathan_compton] 幽默地表示需要一个工具来快速清除桌面上的小部件和视觉噪音。

• [zekenie] 询问该项目支持的操作系统。

• [actinium226] 简单表示赞赏。

• [jdiff] 关注展示视频中的掉帧问题，质疑是QuickShell本身较重，还是系统录制问题，并表示对过渡效果的支持感兴趣。

补充讨论：
• 项目成熟度：[vhantz] 和 [riidom] 都提到了项目的未成熟状态和文档的缺乏。
• 对QML的看法：[vhantz] 和 [0x696C6961] 对QML持积极态度，认为其潜力未被充分挖掘，而 [gr4vityWall] 则希望有更多脚本选项和React生态系统的支持。
• 实际应用：[jp1016] 分享了自己在类似项目中的实际应用经验，提供了另一个视角。
• 技术性能：[jdiff] 对展示视频的技术问题提出了质疑，关注性能和用户体验。

争议焦点：
• QML的使用及其潜力：部分评论认为QML未得到足够重视和利用，而另一些评论则希望有更多脚本选项。
• 技术性能问题：[jdiff] 对展示视频中的掉帧问题提出了质疑，可能涉及QuickShell的性能表现。

data.title: Ratfactor's illustrated guide to folding fitted sheets
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何折叠弹性床单，强调需要耐心学习。作者分享了自己从视频中学会折叠技巧的经历，并详细描述了具体步骤。首先，将床单反铺平整，找到四个角并拉直形成一个近似的长方形，然后分三次折叠长边，再折短边，最后可以用力压成一个小 bundle。尽管步骤简单，但需要反复练习才能掌握。文章还解释了折叠的目标是将弹性部分隐藏起来，形成一个整齐的长方形小包，便于存放。作者用幽默的方式鼓励读者尝试，并提供了历史背景和专利文件以增加趣味性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何处理和存放床单，特别是 fitted sheets 的折叠方法

不同观点：
• **重视折叠并寻求方法**：
  - [SoftTalker] 和 [ctippett] 认为视频和文章提供了有用的指导，帮助解决折叠 fitted sheets 的困难，并对文章的幽默表示欣赏。
  - [binarymax] 赞赏文章和插图的用心。
  - [marai2] 用幽默的方式表达了对教学如何折叠 fitted sheets 的感谢。

• **不在乎折叠效果**：
  - [jakubmazanec] 提到自己折叠 fitted sheets 的方式不美观，但因为收纳时看不到，所以不在意。
  - [Moru] 和 [SilverElfin] 提到自己不折叠床单，洗完直接放回床上或堆在篮子里。
  - [baxuz] 和 [jonstewart] 表示自己只是把床单卷起来或揉成团塞进柜子里。

• **替代方案或极端做法**：
  - [nielsbot] 提出几种替代方案，如雇佣人折叠、购买新的床单并丢弃旧的、或直接不换床单，这些方法带有讽刺意味。
  - [pavel_lishin] 表示完全不在乎折叠 fitted sheets，直接把它们扔进抽屉。

• **个人经验与性别刻板印象**：
  - [snozolli] 分享了自己因为母亲的要求而对折叠 fitted sheets 产生恐惧，但后来发现约会对象并不在意是否折叠得当，只关心床单的清洁。并提出单身汉的 hack 是不需要多套床单。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到的幽默和讽刺（如“恶魔的折纸”和“上帝的工作”）增加了讨论的趣味性。
• 争议的焦点在于是否值得花费精力去折叠 fitted sheets，一些人认为有必要并寻求方法，而另一些人则认为无需在意或有其他更简单的替代方式。

44845839.article_content:
The laundry awaits us all.
Note to the impatient:
You can just scroll down to the drawings of fitted
sheets being folded. You won’t hurt my feelings. (I’ll never even know.) But
you may want to bookmark this page for later instead. You can get fast at
folding fitted sheets. But to
learn
how to fold fitted sheets is going to
take some patience. I do not recommend learning anything, and especially not
anything that involves elastic, when you’re in a hurry.
I used to believe that folding a fitted sheet
was a task improved by an accelerant
(thedoghousediaries.com).
Perhaps you feel this way as well?
Well, one night, I found myself with an unfolded fitted sheet and a half-serious
desire to learn how to fold it once and for all.
Thirty minutes later, I had paused and replayed portions of a video from
Martha Stewart’s old TV show countless times and…​folded the fitted sheet!
Perhaps you, too desire this knowledge? Then join me as I reveal all!
Why we fit the sheets
It is a well-known fact that an ordinary unsecured bed sheet will escape during
the night in the form of a ghost. You will likely find it in the corner the
next morning. Or, if you leave the window open, you may never find it at all!
To solve this problem, elastic was used to to convert a normal sheet into a
creature
which loves nothing more than to hug a bed mattress. A fitted sheet
will happily remain on a mattress for as long as you allow it.
If you like a bit of history, the bottom of this page has some of
that, including
real, downloadable patent files
to keep and enjoy.
Print them out and amaze your friends!
Is it even possible to fold a fitted sheet?
I’m not a topologist. Not even close. But even
I
can take comfort in knowing
that all commercially-available fitted sheets are orientable, two-sided surfaces.
This is in contrast with non-orientable surfaces such as the MÃ¶bius strip,
which is a single surface with a boundary, or a Klein bottle, which doesn’t
even have a boundary.
You can fold a MÃ¶bius strip all you want, but you’ll never get rid of that
twist. If you fold a Klein bottle, you’ll make Clifford Stoll sad.
But a fitted sheet - it can be tamed! It can be folded!
Let’s prove it with a practical demonstration.
The first, and most obvious observation is that a fitted sheet makes a nice,
neat rectangle when it is spread over a mattress.
This leads to the most obvious
insight
: If you flip the sheet over and pull
the corners of the sheet to the corners of the mattress, the "bottom" of the
turned-over sheet makes that same reasonably neat rectangle.
A rectangle of cloth can be folded like paper, even if the inner elastic
makes it a particularly hell-spawned paper.
Understanding this leads to a simple, but tedious method of folding a fitted sheet.
A simple, but tedious method
Lay the fitted sheet neatly upside-down (troublesome ruffled elastic center on the top) so that it’s fully flat on a sheet-sized surface such as a bed. Or the floor. Or outside in the road, what do I care, it’s your sheet.
Then:
Find the corners of the sheet and tug and tease them until the corners and edges form a pretty decent rectangle. It won’t be perfect because the elastic will always pull it a little round.
Fold a third of the sheet down. Smooth it down as if it were paper.
Fold the second third. Keep flattening and smoothing.
Fold the sheet the short direction in thirds. (In spreadsheet terms, we did rows, now we’re doing columns.)
Give a kick in the style of a martial arts expert for the final fold so that the sheet is now a small, subdued bundle.
Celebrate by standing on the vanquished sheet with arms raised in victory. This will further compact the bundle for storage. (Clean feet only!)
Folding a fitted sheet by laying it out upside-down on the bed was the first
method I
completely understood
, but it was very slow and required the
entire surface of the bed. I had to keep walking around the bed to get at the
opposite corners.
In other words, it’s simple, but not easy, in the sense described by software
developer
Hajime Hoshi
(hajimehoshi.com):
Easy:
how quickly you can achieve what you want
Simple:
how quickly you can understand the model
As savvy sheet folders have known for a long time, arm-based corner-gathering
methods aren’t as quick to learn, but they’re much faster…​once you
understand what you’re doing and get the hang of the movements!
The initial goal
Of course, the
ultimate
goal is to turn the fitted sheet into a small,
roughly rectangular bundle that can sit neatly on a shelf.
But the
first
goal of folding a fitted sheet is to turn it into some sort of
foldable rectangle with the elastic on the
inside
. This will allow you to
enveloped the elastic safely away from sight and mind.
Here’s a
half sheet
with the corner pockets paired up at the top:
And here’s a
quarter sheet
with all four pockets together at the top left:
Since both the half and quarter sheets give you roughly rectangular shapes with
the elastic inside, both are perfectly valid folding

data.title: A CT scanner reveals surprises inside the 386 processor's ceramic package
data.author: robin_reala
data.article_summary: 英特尔于1985年发布了386处理器，这是x86系列中的首款32位芯片。该芯片封装在一个带有132个金镀引脚的陶瓷方块中，这些引脚与主板上的插座连接。通过3D CT扫描揭示了芯片内部的复杂结构，其中包括六层复杂的布线。芯片采用132针陶瓷封装，以满足高针数、良好散热和低噪声电源的需求。封装内部类似一个六层的陶瓷印刷电路板，通过金 bond wires将硅芯片与封装的焊盘连接。制作过程包括陶瓷片加工、钨膏布线、层压和高温烧结，最后安装芯片并进行封装和测试。电源层和信号层通过金属迹线和过孔连接，以确保电气性能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕旧计算机硬件、芯片封装、引脚配置及相关技术问题的讨论。

不同观点：
• **[mlhpdx]** 提到对后期芯片包的热-机械循环疲劳进行了分析，通过CAD、有限元分析（FEA）和实证测试发现大多数情况下这不是大问题。但仍不建议博物馆每天对旧PC进行电源循环。
• **[mike50]** 认为将混合封装信息公开非常有价值，尤其是对新手工程师而言。他还指出，现代布线不如旧军用混合器件复杂，虽然有六层，但只有一个整体层。
• **[lisbbb]** 分享了个人经历，提到在1989年左右的电脑展上购买386 DX 25MHz电脑的经历，并描述了这次升级对当时电脑性能的显著提升。
• **[m104]** 认为关于16引脚的保守做法反映了早期公司决策中的某些奇怪假设，这些假设在后来被淘汰以实现理性发展。

44848293.article_content:
Intel released the 386 processor in 1985, the first 32-bit chip in the x86 line.
This chip was packaged in a ceramic square with 132 gold-plated pins protruding from the underside, fitting into
a socket on the motherboard.
While this package may seem boring, a lot more is going on inside it than you might expect.
Lumafield
performed a 3-D CT scan of the chip for me, revealing six layers of complex
wiring hidden inside the ceramic package.
Moreover, the chip has nearly invisible metal wires connected to the
sides
of the package, the spikes below.
The scan also revealed that the 386 has two separate power and ground networks: one for I/O and one for the CPU's logic.
A CT scan of the 386 package. The ceramic package doesn't show up in this image, but it encloses the spiky wires.
The package, below, provides no hint of the complex wiring embedded inside the ceramic.
The silicon die is normally not visible, but I removed the square metal lid that covers it.
1
As a result, you can also see the two tiers of gold contacts that surround the silicon die.
The 386 package with the lid over the die removed.
Intel selected the 132-pin ceramic package to meet the requirements of a high pin count, good thermal characteristics,
and low-noise power to the die.
2
:
However, standard packages didn't provide sufficient power, so Intel designed a custom package with
"single-row double shelf bonding to two signal layers and four power and ground planes."
In other words, the die's bond wires are connected to the two shelves (or tiers) of pads surrounding the die.
Internally, the package is like a 6-layer printed-circuit board made from ceramic.
Package cross-section. Redrawn from "High Performance Technology, Circuits and Packaging for the 80386".
The photo below shows the two tiers of pads with tiny gold bond wires attached: I measured the bond wires at 35 µm in diameter, thinner than a typical human hair.
Some pads have up to five wires attached to support more current for the power and ground pads.
You can consider the package to be a hierarchical interface from the tiny circuits on the die to the
much larger features of the computer's motherboard.
Specifically, the die has a feature size of 1 µm,
while the metal wiring on top of the die has 6 µm spacing.
The chip's wiring connects to the chip's bond pads, which have 0.01" spacing (.25 mm).
The bond wires connect to the package's pads, which have 0.02" spacing (.5 mm); double the spacing because there are two tiers.
The package connects these pads to the pin grid with 0.1" spacing (2.54 mm).
Thus, the scale expands by about a factor of 2500 from the die's microscopic circuitry to the chip's pins.
`
Close-up of the bond wires.
The ceramic package is manufactured through a complicated process.
4
The process starts with flexible ceramic "green sheets", consisting of ceramic powder mixed with a binding agent.
After holes for vias are created in the sheet, tungsten paste is silk-screened onto the sheet to form the wiring.
The sheets are stacked, laminated under pressure, and then sintered at high temperature (1500ºC to 1600ºC)
to create the rigid ceramic.
The pins are brazed onto the bottom of the chip.
Next, the pins and the inner contacts for the die are electroplated with gold.
3
The die is mounted, gold bond wires are attached, and a metal cap is soldered over the die to encapsulate it.
Finally, the packaged chip is tested, the package is labeled, and the chip is ready to be sold.
The diagram below shows a close-up of a signal layer inside the package.
The pins are connected to the package's shelf pads through metal traces, spectacularly colored in the CT scan.
(These traces are surprisingly wide and free-form; I expected narrower traces to reduce capacitance.)
Bond wires connect the shelf pads to the bond pads on the silicon die.
(The die image is added to the diagram; it is not part of the CT scan.)
The large red circles are vias from the pins. Some vias connect to this signal layer, while other vias pass through to
other layers.
The smaller red circles are connections to a power layer; because the shelf pads are only on the two signal layers,
the six power planes have connections to the signal layers for bonding.
Since bond wires are only connected on the signal layers, the power layers need connections to pads on the signal
layers.
A close-up of a signal layer. The die image is pasted in.
The diagram below shows the corresponding portion of a power layer.
A power layer looks completely different from a signal layer; it is a single conductive plane with holes.
The grid of smaller holes allows the ceramic above and below this layer to bond, forming a solid piece of ceramic.
The larger holes surround pin vias (red dots), allowing pin connections to pass through to a different layer.
The red dots that contact the sheet are where power pins connect to this layer.

data.title: Which colors are primary?
data.author: Michelangelo11
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：颜色的基本原理及其在不同领域中的应用

不同观点：
• chowells认为，文章没有提到人类和其他动物的眼睛生物学基础，不同动物可能对其他颜色更敏感，虽然这对文章的主题不重要，但他强调这些颜色并没有神奇之处，只是因为它们能有效刺激人眼的颜色受体。
• quitit指出，艺术家和艺术教师并不会真正坚持三原色可以混合出所有颜色，实际绘画中会使用更多颜色，且常使用如“暖红”“冷蓝”等术语，以解决颜色有限的问题，并在专业印刷中引入如Pantone系统等额外颜色。
• iambateman表示，作为成年人理解到颜色并非相互衍生而来感到震惊，并认为将色轮作为“真正的轮”来教可能更合理，但同时承认“三原色是个社会建构”的说法在社交中可能不受欢迎。
• kens提到，英语中有11个基本颜色术语，因此试图教青色和洋红色作为原色比教蓝和红要困难得多。
• hinkley以科幻作品为例，讨论颜色并非普遍一致，不同生物可能感知不同颜色，并提出元素的发光颜色可能作为基础颜色，且建议在高级科学交流中使用更复杂的颜色概念。
• esafak建议通过色度图来理解加色原色，指出通过混合原色来生成颜色，并强调需要至少三个原色来封闭色域。
• fanf2补充，颜色感知不仅依赖视网膜的锥细胞，还涉及视觉皮层的对立过程，这是幼儿园三原色的来源。
• DarkNova6表示，在中欧生活中从未遇到认为黄色是原色的人，对此感到困惑。

补充讨论：
• LynxInLA提到文章作者是《Dinotopia》系列书籍的创作者，提供了背景信息。
• zuluonezero推荐了Gurney的《Color and Light》一书，作为艺术家对颜色的深度探讨。
• euroderf和vladmk简短地提到人眼对某些颜色的感知，未深入展开。

争议焦点：
• 关于三原色的定义和实际应用存在争议，quitit和DarkNova6等用户质疑传统三原色在实际艺术和日常使用中的有效性和普遍性。
• 不同领域（如艺术和科学）对颜色的理解和应用方式不同，导致对原色的选择和定义存在分歧。

总结：讨论围绕颜色的生物学基础、艺术应用、社会建构以及不同领域对颜色的不同理解展开，并涉及颜色感知、色轮教学以及具体颜色例子的争论。

data.title: An AI-first program synthesis framework built around a new programming language
data.author: tosh
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种由Erik Meijer提出的AI驱动、以程序合成为核心的框架，使用一种名为Universalis的新编程语言。该语言专为知识工作者设计，易于阅读和操作，能够在Automind神经计算机上执行，并配有相关工具进行分析和修改。Universalis的命名灵感来自17世纪哲学家莱布尼茨的“普遍科学”理念，旨在协调所有人类知识。该语言注重代码的可读性，而非传统编程语言的语法结构，使其更接近自然语言，便于非专业开发者理解和使用。例如，通过简单的自然语言问题，AI可以生成相应的Universalis代码并计算结果，如计算利润率。与传统编程不同，Universalis旨在让机器编写代码，人类只需阅读，降低了使用门槛，促进了AI技术的广泛应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Universalis语言及其相关技术（如Kotlin DataFrames、编译器插件、LLM应用）的实现、实用性、简化编程的潜力及局限。

不同观点：
• **对新技术演示的积极评价**：
   - [gavinray] 对Kotlin Conf 2025上展示的编译器插件表示赞赏，尤其是对DataFrame表达式的即席类型推断功能。他指出这种功能类似于TypeScript的类型推断，能在JVM语言中实现类似的效果。
  
• **对文章准确性和现实性的质疑**：
   - [duskwuff] 认为文章描述不准确，语法示例不一致，控制结构用英文描述，且示例中使用了类似"toPdf()"的全自动函数。质疑文章内容是否真实反映了某种可用语言，还是仅仅是与ChatGPT的互动。
  
• **对技术演进历史的评论**：
   - [pjmlp] 提到Universalis与Haskell和LINQ的历史关联，暗示这是Erik Meijer的最新关注点，将其置于编程语言发展的背景中。

• **对技术复杂性和未来发展的担忧**：
   - [rvasa] 认为虽然新技术初期可能简单易用，但随着需求增加，最终会重新引入复杂的编程概念（如函数复用、类型、状态机、并发等）。他对新技术能否应对大规模复杂问题持观望态度。

• **对文章宣传性及技术局限的批评**：
   - [AIPedant] 认为文章像广告，未讨论技术的缺点和局限。特别指出LLM在处理复杂问题时的错误率更高，对文章中“减轻认知负担”的说法感到不满，认为应展示处理稍复杂问题的能力。

• **对简化编程的潜在负面影响的担忧**：
   - [ethanwillis] 质疑让编程变得更简单是否是好事，担心这会导致更多低质量代码的出现。

• **对技术民主化潜力的积极评价**：
   - [sys13] 支持通过AI技术让编程更普及，认为保持人类主导地位很重要，尽管目前的语法可能仍显繁琐。

44847334.article_content:
Current Issue
Past Issues
Topics
July 7, 2025
Volume 23, issue 3
PDF
Unleashing the Power
of End-User Programmable AI
Creating an AI-first program Synthesis framework
Erik Meijer
As a demonstration of what can be accomplished with contemporary LLMs (large language models), this paper outlines the high-level design of an AI-first, program-synthesis framework built around a new programming language, Universalis, designed for knowledge workers to read, optimized for our neural computer (
Automind
; queue.acm.org) to execute, and ready to be analyzed and manipulated by an accompanying set of tools. We call the language Universalis in honor of Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz, a 17th century German polymath who had an amazing vision long before our time. Leibniz's centuries-old program of a universal science (
scientia universalis
; wikipedia.org) for coordinating all human knowledge into a systematic whole comprises two parts: (1) a universal
notation
(
characteristica universalis
; oxfordreference.com) by use of which any item of information whatsoever can be recorded naturally and systematically, and (2) a means of manipulating the knowledge thus recorded in a computational fashion, to reveal its logical interrelations and consequences (
calculus ratiocinator
; wikipedia.org). Exactly what current day LLMs provide!
This may sound a bit abstract and academic, but it is extremely concrete and practical. Here is an example of a question that can be asked in natural language (the
what
):
Question
Alice bought a kilo of apples for $[@B]. She sold them for $[@S]. How much percent %[@P] profit or loss did Alice make?
This is the generated Universalis implementation (the
how
):
Answer
The apples cost $[@B], and the selling price was $[@S], so Alice made a profit of $[@D is (@S-@B)].The profit percentage is therefore [@P is (@D/@B)*100)]%.
While this may seem like a whimsical example, it is not intrinsically easier or harder for an AI model compared to solving a real-world problem from a human perspective. The model processes both simple and complex problems using the same underlying mechanism. To lessen the cognitive load for the human reader, however, we will stick to simple targeted examples in this article.
To actually run a Universalis program, users need to be able to enter initial values for variables and view the values of computed variables. Depending on the environment in which Universalis code runs, the user interface can vary. Assuming a spreadsheet-style "live programming" environment where you can toggle between showing formulas and showing values, setting
@B=10
and
@S=17
,
@P=70
and the code renders as follows:
Question
Alice bought a kilo of apples for $[10]. She sold them for $[17]. How much percent %[70] profit or loss did Alice make?
Answer
The apples cost $[10], and the selling price was $[17], so Alice made a profit of $[7 is (17-10)].The profit percentage is therefore [70 is (7/10)*100)]%.
Unlike traditional programming languages, which prioritize syntax and structure optimized for writing by professional developers, Universalis is designed with the philosophy that
code should be read by domain experts and written by machines
.
This design tradeoff means that Universalis scripts are structured in a way that closely resembles natural language, making them intuitive and accessible even to those without formal programming training. A simple language reduces the complexity that an AI model needs to handle, making it easier for the model to generate accurate and error-free code. This shift in focus from writing to reading represents a significant departure from conventional programming paradigms, paving the way for a more inclusive and user-friendly approach to harnessing the power of AI.
Think of Universalis clauses as some kind of literate Excel spreadsheet formulas such as
[@D is (@S-@B)]
over named tables, or relations, enclosed in
hedges
surrounded by natural language explanation, where
cells
in the table correspond to variables such as
@B
,
@S
, and
@D
(figure 1).
The main goal in designing Universalis was that any user who can write basic Excel formulas should be able to understand Universalis scripts. Technically, Universalis is based on Prolog, and code fragments inside [...] hedges are logic predicates.
You can also optionally specify, or let Automind generate, pre-conditions that are checked
before
the code is run by Automind:
[@B>0] The buying price [@B] per kilo of apples must be greater than [0], implying that Alice paid a positive amount for the apples.
[@S>=0] The selling price [@S] per kilo of apples must be non-negative, implying that Alice did not give away the apples for free and there was no scenario where she had to pay to dispose of them.
and post-conditions that are checked after Automind has run the code:
If [@S >= @B], then the profit percentage [@P] should be non-negative, indicating a profit or break-even situation.
If [@S < @B], then the profit percentage [@P] should be negative,
44847334.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种由Erik Meijer提出的AI驱动、以程序合成为核心的框架，使用一种名为Universalis的新编程语言。该语言专为知识工作者设计，易于阅读和操作，能够在Automind神经计算机上执行，并配有相关工具进行分析和修改。Universalis的命名灵感来自17世纪哲学家莱布尼茨的“普遍科学”理念，旨在协调所有人类知识。该语言注重代码的可读性，而非传统编程语言的语法结构，使其更接近自然语言，便于非专业开发者理解和使用。例如，通过简单的自然语言问题，AI可以生成相应的Universalis代码并计算结果，如计算利润率。与传统编程不同，Universalis旨在让机器编写代码，人类只需阅读，降低了使用门槛，促进了AI技术的广泛应用。

data.title: Testing Bitchat at the music festival
data.author: alexcos
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：去中心化消息传递的可行性与技术挑战

不同观点：
• **去中心化消息传递的潜力与现实挑战**：  
  - **teucris**：认为去中心化消息传递的理念很扎实，但在蓝牙可靠性、平台差异、达到有效中继的关键用户数量方面存在许多障碍。尽管想法很好，但技术实现困难，导致无法广泛应用。  
  - **SeanAnderson**：引用自己尝试使用FireChat的经历，指出进展缓慢，但计划在Burning Man活动上再次尝试使用mesh网络，希望通过专用硬件改善连接可靠性。

• **对现有解决方案的批评与期望**：  
  - **cedws**：对Bitchat等个体开发的应用持怀疑态度，认为这些只是早期 hobby 项目，难以在广泛场景中应用。主张需要一个标准化的协议，由制造商普遍实施，例如Apple的Find My网络。  
  - **kawfey**：虽然认为蓝牙和WiFi消息应用效果不佳，但指出专用硬件（如Gotenna、Beartooth）表现较好，强调硬件解决方案比软件更有效。

• **技术细节与改进建议**：  
  - **cakealert**：指出传统智能手机的限制，需要root权限才能实现某些技术（如监听数据包和跳频）。  
  - **Catbert59**：分享了在工业产品中使用BLE Meshing的经验，指出多跳和流量增加会导致不稳定，认为TCP协议在这种环境下可能不适用。  
  - **nullc**：提出使用store&forward和高效的调和机制来改善mesh网络的可靠性，并分享了相关的GitHub库，建议将时间划分为适当的小周期以保持消息同步。

• **用户体验与界面设计**：  
  - **godelski**：关注用户界面设计，特别是暗色模式的默认设置，认为开发者不应忽视用户对暗色主题的需求。

• **幽默与讽刺**：  
  - **yobid20** 和 **monster_truck**：以幽默的方式表达对蓝牙技术的不满，认为效果不如其他原始手段（如烟雾信号）。  
  - **diimdeep**：幻想如果世界没有WiFi和蓝牙芯片，只有蜂窝模组和API，生活可能会更好。  
  - **specproc**：引用xkcd漫画，以幽默方式总结了讨论主题。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：去中心化消息传递的技术可行性与实际应用之间的差距，特别是在蓝牙和WiFi技术上的局限性。不同用户对现有应用（如Bitchat、FireChat）的有效性有不同看法，部分用户对技术实现持悲观态度，认为需要更标准化的解决方案和专用硬件支持。

• **潜在解决方案**：通过专用硬件（如Gotenna、Beartooth）和store&forward机制，有可能改善去中心化消息传递的可靠性和性能。

data.title: ChatGPT 5 is slow and no better than 4
data.author: iwontberude
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPT-5的性能表现及其与之前版本（如GPT-4o）的对比，涉及其在不同应用场景中的表现、速度问题、用户体验以及营销宣传与实际体验的差距。

不同观点：
• **GPT-5未达预期**：[dileeparanawake] 认为GPT-5并没有像宣传中那样带来巨大改变，某些方面甚至比GPT-4更差、更慢，尤其是在代码和学习方面。他还提到，模型的扩展似乎遇到了瓶颈，现在需要关注的是“每瓦特的价值”，即更小、更高效的模型。

• **GPT-5在对话中的成熟表现**：[labrador] 认为GPT-5作为对话思考伙伴优于GPT-4o，回答更简洁、信息更集中，对话更加流畅，且语气更加专业。虽然有人可能怀念GPT-4o的奉承式对话风格，但[labrador] 更喜欢现在的专业风格。

• **GPT-5在代码和反应速度上的改进**：[hirvi74] 发现GPT-5在代码生成上的成功率有所提高，且在回答 trivial 问题时更加简洁。不过，他提到对$200/月的计划与其他版本的比较存在疑问。

• **GPT-5速度变慢但质量提升**：[al_borland] 认为尽管GPT-5速度变慢，但若其能减少后续跟进问题的数量，整体效率还是提升的。同时，相较于手动研究，GPT-5仍然快得多。

• **API速度问题及解决方法**：[pseudo_meta] 发现GPT-5的API明显变慢，通过调整reasoning effort设置可以改善速度问题，但需要切换到新的Response API，这带来了一些额外工作。

• **GPT-5在不同模型和应用中的差异**：[Tiberium] 提到GPT-5在API中表现优于GPT-4o，尤其在网页设计和编程方面，但在Chat模型中表现较差。还指出，GPT-5的实际表现受模型路由影响，订阅Pro版本才能获得最佳体验。

• **对旧模型的依赖与失去**：[darepublic] 和 [gooodvibes] 都对失去GPT-4o感到不满，认为用户应有权选择使用旧模型，直接取消4o对用户体验造成了负面影响。

• **对OpenAI不透明的批评**：[rolodexter2023] 批评OpenAI越来越不透明，称GPT-5可能只是营销噱头，且越来越像一个“黑盒”。

• **API使用中的性能问题**：[binarymax] 提到在API中大规模运行任务时，GPT-5速度非常慢，处理简单任务的时间相较GPT-4o也显著增加。

• **Pro版本的优异表现**：[mikert89] 则对GPT-5的Pro版本给予高度评价，认为其表现“不可思议”。

补充讨论：
• **合成数据的影响**：[dileeparanawake] 提到GPT-5使用合成数据训练，但这可能导致其在实际任务中表现不佳，强调合成数据的质量对模型训练至关重要。

• **争议焦点**：GPT-5是否真正比GPT-4o有显著提升，特别是在速度和实用性方面，用户体验和营销宣传之间的差距引发了较多争议。

data.title: The Framework Desktop is a beast
data.author: lemonberry
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了Framework Desktop台式电脑的优异性能和独特设计。该电脑体积小巧（4.5升），运行安静，即使在高负载下也无噪音。它采用了AMD Ryzen AI Max 395+处理器，适合小型机身，性能卓越，尤其在多核工作负载下表现突出，比Beelink SER8和SER9更快。相比苹果M4 Max和M4 Pro，其多核性能分别快40%和50%。尽管在单核性能上不如苹果，但在实际使用中差异不大。Framework Desktop在价格上也具有优势，64GB RAM和2TB NVMe的配置售价1,876美元，而类似规格的Mac Studio售价高达3,299美元。总体而言，Framework Desktop在性能和性价比上都非常出色，尤其适合开发者使用Docker等多核工作流程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AMD RDNA 架构、硬件设备的选择与比较、Framework Desktop的评价与性价比、Linux在企业环境中的应用、AI工作负载与硬件兼容性

不同观点：
• [Archit3ch] 认为 RDNA 3.5 缺乏 Matrix Cores（类似于Nvidia的Tensor Cores），而这些硬件加速器在机器学习（ML）工作负载中将变得越来越重要。相比之下，Nvidia在2022年推出了带有Tensor Cores的消费级显卡，而AMD的RDNA 4要到2025年才会在桌面端推出。对非ML工作负载的影响尚不确定。

• [paolomainardi] 关注的是在企业环境中，Linux系统缺乏类似Apple硬件中固件级远程设备管理的功能，认为这是阻碍Linux在企业中推广的主要障碍。

• [lvl155] 建议AMD推出更高性能的桌面级芯片，并提出将两个桌面级芯片放在一块主板上的设想，以提高计算能力。

• [ilaksh] 对Framework Desktop和GMKtec AI Mini Ryzen AI Max+ 395 128GB mini PC进行了比较，质疑两者在硬件和价格上的差异，并询问是否有人进行过直接对比。

• [Kirth] 对AMD芯片与M4 Max的比较感到困惑，不确定这是否意味着AMD芯片在性能上已经达到同等水平，以及这对设备上的LLM（大语言模型）意味着什么。

• [politelemon] 对Framework Desktop以较低价格实现高性能表示好奇，并询问为什么普通用户无法通过类似方式在PCPartPicker上组装出类似的机器。

• [jamesgill] 对Framework Desktop持批评态度，认为其更像是一种噱头营销，性价比不高，且没有显著区别于其他桌面电脑的特点。

• [fmajid] 取消了Framework Desktop的订单，转而购买HP Z2 Mini G1a，原因是希望替代Mac Studio，并对Apple的软件质量不满。虽然HP更贵，但具备ECC RAM和10G Ethernet等优势。

• [ashleyn] 关注AMD GPU在生成式AI工作流中的兼容性问题，认为目前大多数AI工作流都依赖于CUDA，AMD GPU在这方面可能存在劣势。

• [kristianp] 提到Framework Desktop的图形卡具有一定的灵活性，可以通过移动主板到不同机箱并使用PCIe插槽来安装外部GPU，但高性能显卡可能会受到带宽限制。

• [damonll] 建议在Mac上使用Orbstack作为引擎以获得更好的性能，认为这比Docker快至少两倍。

• [Xenoamorphous] 表达了对硬件评测和性能指标（如bogomips）的不在乎，可能代表了一部分不关注技术细节的用户观点。

• [ThinkBeat] 认为相关评论像广告，可能对内容的真实性或偏向性表示怀疑。

• [Jtsummers] 对Framework Desktop的定位提出质疑，认为在桌面电脑市场，用户已经有很多选择，而Framework Desktop在可修复性方面不如其笔记本产品，甚至不如其他桌面电脑。这与其DIY梦制造商的品牌形象不符。

• [dustingetz] 认为Framework Desktop在2000美元的价位上提供了相当高的计算性能。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点：Framework Desktop的性价比和定位是讨论中的一个争议点。部分用户（如jamesgill）认为其更像噱头，而其他用户（如dustingetz）则认为在这个价位上性能出色。
• 不同设备间的比较：多个评论提到了不同硬件设备之间的比较，如Framework Desktop与GMKtec mini PC、HP Z2 Mini等，显示出用户在选择硬件时的多样化需求和考虑因素。
• AMD与Nvidia在硬件加速器上的差距：Archit3ch强调了AMD在硬件加速器方面的落后，而Nvidia和Apple已经在这方面有了显著进展，可能影响未来ML工作负载的表现。

44841262.article_content:
August  7, 2025
The Framework Desktop is a beast
I've been running the
Framework Desktop
for a few months here in Copenhagen now. It's an incredible machine. It's completely quiet, even under heavy, stress-all-cores load. It's tiny too, at just 4.5L of volume, especially compared to my old beautiful but bulky North tower running the 7950X — yet it's faster! And finally, it's simply funky, quirky, and fun!
In some ways, the Framework Desktop is a curious machine. Desktop PCs are already very user-repairable! So why is Framework even bringing their talents to this domain? In the laptop realm, they're basically alone with that concept, but in the desktop space, it's rather crowded already. Yet it somehow still makes sense.
Partly because Framework has gone with the AMD Ryzen AI Max 395+, which is technically a laptop CPU. You can find it in the ASUS ROG Flow Z13 and the HP ZBook Ultra. Which means it'll fit in a tiny footprint, and Framework apparently just wanted to see what they could do in that form factor. They clearly had fun with it. Look at mine:
There are 21 little tiles on the front that you can get in a bunch of different colors or with logos from Framework. Or you can 3D print your own! It's a welcome change in aesthetic from the brushed aluminum or gamer-focused RGBs approach that most of the competition is taking.
But let's cut to the benchmarks. That's really why you'd buy a machine like the Framework Desktop. There are significantly cheaper mini PCs available from Beelink and others, but so far, Framework has the only AMD 395+ unit on sale that's completely silent (the GMKTec very much is not, nor is the Z3 Flow). And for me, that's just a dealbreaker. I can't listen to roaring fans anymore.
Here's the key benchmark for me:
That's the only type of multi-core workload I really sit around waiting on these days, and the Framework Desktop absolutely crushes it. It's almost twice as fast as the Beelink SER8 and still a solid third faster than the Beelink SER9 too. Of course, it's also a lot more expensive, but you're clearly getting some multi-core bang for your buck here!
It's even a more dramatic difference to the Macs. It's a solid 40% faster than the M4 Max and 50% faster than the M4 Pro! Now some will say "that's just because Docker is faster on Linux," and they're not entirely wrong. Docker runs natively on Linux, so for this test, where the MySQL/Redis/ElasticSearch data stores run in Docker while Ruby and the app code runs natively, that's part of the answer. Last I checked, it was about 25% of the difference.
But so what? Docker is an integral part of the workflow for tons of developers. We use it to be able to run different versions of MySQL, Redis, and ElasticSearch for different applications on the same machine at the same time. You can't really do that without Docker. So this is what Real World benchmarks reveal.
It's not just about having a Docker advantage, though. The AMD 395+ is also incredibly potent in RAW CPU performance. Those 16 Zen5 cores are running at 5.1GHz, and in Geekbench 6 multicore, this is how they stack up:
Basically matching the M4 Max! And a good chunk faster than the M4 Pro (as well as other AMDs and Intel's 14900K!). No wonder that it's crazy quick with a full-core stress test like running 30,000 assertions for our
HEY
test suite.
To be fair, the M4s are faster in single-core performance. Apple holds the crown there. It's about 20%. And you'll see that in benchmarks like Speedometer, which mostly measures JavaScript single-core performance. The Framework Desktop puts out 670 vs 744 on the M4 Pro on Speedometer 2.1. On SP 3.1, it's an even bigger difference with 35 vs 50.
But I've found that all these computers feel fast enough in single-core performance these days. I can't actually feel the difference browsing on a machine that does 670 vs 744 on SP2.1. Hell, I can barely feel the difference between the SER8, which does 506, and the M4 Pro! The only time I actually feel like I'm waiting on anything is in multi-core workloads like the HEY test suite, and here the AMD 395+ is very near the fastest you can get for a consumer desktop machine today at any price.
It gets even better when you bring price into the equation, though. The Framework Desktop with 64GB RAM + 2TB NVMe is $1,876. To get a Mac Studio with similar specs — M4 Max, 64GB RAM, 2TB NVMe — you'll literally spend nearly twice as much at $3,299! If you go for 128GB RAM, you'll spend $2,276 on the Framework, but $4,099 on the Mac. And it'll still be way slower for development work using Docker! The Framework Desktop is simply a great deal.
Speaking of 64GB vs 128GB, I've been running the 64GB version, and I almost never get anywhere close to the limits. I think the highest I've seen in regular use is about 20GB of RAM in action. Linux is really efficient. Especially when you're using a window manager like Hyprland, as we do in Omarchy.

data.title: Caligra Workbench
data.author: phanimahesh
data.article_summary: Caligra Workbench是一款基于Linux®的操作系统，专为技术工作站设计，旨在提高开发人员效率，减少干扰。它具有高性能用户界面，支持商业级媒体和设备管理，适合安全和主权部署。系统采用rpm核心，用户可通过dnf和homebrew添加软件包，兼容Fedora项目和其它发行版工具。Workbench专注于加速工作流程，提供多种快捷键和窗口管理功能，如Teleport和Stash，帮助用户快速导航和记录信息。该系统适用于Caligra c100开发终端，售价1999美元，将于1月26日发货。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[Caligra "developer terminal"及其Linux发行版的定位、设计和市场策略]

不同观点：
• [visviva] 认为宣传内容缺乏细节，显得可疑或至少令人困惑。
• [ugh123] 指出其设计类似现代版Commodore 64，但对整体设置表示困惑，尤其是“Workbench”作为简化桌面环境的定位。
• [pjmlp] 批评该Linux发行版受到过多苹果设计的影响，偏离了Linux的传统风格。
• [satertek] 质疑其市场定位，认为System76已经占据了类似的小众市场。
• [type0] 提到名称与Calligra Suite的混淆问题，建议改名以避免误导现有Linux用户。
• [garciansmith] 对其键盘布局和符号表示困惑，认为设计既有趣又糟糕。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点包括设计风格（是否过于苹果化）、市场定位（是否与现有产品重叠）以及名称混淆问题。
• 键盘布局和符号设计引发了用户的混合反应，既有兴趣也有批评。

data.title: Isle FPGA Computer: creating a simple, open, modern computer
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary: "Isle FPGA Computer"介绍了一个名为Isle的简易开源计算机项目，旨在鼓励个人通过FPGA开发板和模拟器自行设计和实验。Isle采用32位RISC-V CPU，具备2D图形引擎、Unicode文本模式、声音支持、SD卡存储、键盘和鼠标输入，以及用于扩展的虚拟插槽。其操作系统和软件尽量自研，同时保持与外部世界的互操作性。项目强调简单性和现代性，使用当代组件和开发工具，并从硬件和软件两方面并行开发。Isle的名字寓意着隔离与实验，希望促成多种各具特色的小型计算机共同发展。目前项目处于早期阶段，主要聚焦于硬件开发。感兴趣者可通过赞助获取最新进展并参与其中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同技术方案和选择在硬件项目中的应用，包括显示分辨率和处理器选择。

不同观点：
• Western0认为每个字需要10位，可能还需要额外2位用于错误纠正。这表明了对数据传输准确性和效率的关注，尤其是在处理低级数据编码时。

• Jecel指出在实际测试中，许多显示器无法正常显示640x480的分辨率，但所有测试的显示器都能在1280x768分辨率下正常工作。因此，jecel决定在项目中改用后者，反映了在硬件兼容性和实际应用中的实际问题。

• OrvalWintermute支持使用64bit RISC5处理器，强调其在计算效率、地址空间和性能上的优势，尤其是在高性能和复杂系统中的应用。他还提到RISC5的价格优势和未来适应性，并提供了不同型号处理器的价格对比，显示了对性价比和硬件性能的关注。

补充讨论：
• WillFlux作为Project F博客的作者，表示愿意回答问题。虽然没有直接提出观点，但显示了对讨论的开放态度和支持。

争议焦点：
• 显示分辨率的选择：jecel的经验显示640x480分辨率在许多显示器上无法正常工作，而Western0可能在考虑较低分辨率下的位深度需求。这反映了理论需求和实际硬件表现之间的差异。

44807603.article_content:
Isle FPGA Computer
Published 01 Aug 2025 (DRAFT)
Be not afeard; the isle is full of noises,
Sounds, and sweet airs, that give delight and hurt not.
Shakespeare,
The Tempest
I'm creating a computer called
Isle
. In this post, I'll introduce you to Isle and hope to inspire you to come on a journey with me and build your own computer. This introduction is still in draft and will evolve as Isle evolves.
Isle is a simple, modern computer â an open design that encourages tinkering, experimentation, and doing your own thing. By simple, I mean that one person can understand the whole system. Modern in that we use contemporary components, development tools, and standards. The design isn't finished, so the specification is naturally uncertain, but the following should give you a rough idea.
Isle Specification
32-bit RISC-V CPU
2D Graphics Engine
Unicode Text Mode
Sound
SD Card Storage
Keyboard and Mouse
Virtual Slots for Expansion
Isle OS and Simple Software
Everything is as homegrown as practical while retaining interoperability with the wider world. For example, the graphics system is a custom design, but it works with regular TVs and computer displays. I've chosen a RISC-V CPU, rather than design my own architecture. RISC-V lets us use the full panoply of modern programming languages and development tools while remaining simple. We'll develop software in parallel with our hardware, beginning with RISC-V assembler and adding high-level languages later.
I'm not building PCBs or selling hardware; I'm using existing FPGA dev boards and simulators. Think of an FPGA as a giant virtual breadboard or Lego for hardware design. With a simulator, you don't even need a dev board; you can run your hardware on your existing PC or Mac with free software.
Why call it Isle? Aren't islands isolated and cut off? To some extent, the isolation is the point, a refuge from the complex, bloated, engagement-driven technology that we live with every day. But islands are also a place of experimentation and evolution. Look at
Darwin's finches
, the
Komodo dragon
, and
coco de mer
. I hope to inspire an archipelago of small computers, each with its own personality and style, but with enough common ground to share designs and ideas.
I believe graphics and sound are central to what makes computers fun to program and tinker with. I also believe in learning by doing. So, let's introduce the dev boards and get to work on the graphics hardware.
Special thanks to my
sponsors
who've stuck with me as I've developed this project:
Daniel Cliche
,
David C. Norris
,
dvir
,
Justin Finkelstein
,
kromych
,
Martin Young
,
Matt Venn
,
Michael Doornbos
,
Paul Sajna
,
Renaldas Zioma
, and those who wish to remain anonymous.
You can
sponsor me
to support Isle development and get early access to new chapters and designs.
Next step:
Dev Boards
or
Isle Index
PS. It's still early days for the project, and I'm currently focused on hardware. If you're looking to jump into RISC-V and software, you'll need to be patient for a few months.

data.title: Who got arrested in the raid on the XSS crime forum?
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: 2025年7月22日，欧洲刑警组织宣布，在一项由法国警方主导的长期调查后，一名38岁的男子在基辅被捕，该男子是俄罗斯网络犯罪论坛XSS的管理员。XSS拥有超过5万名成员，该行动引发了论坛成员的猜测和恐慌。被捕者疑似是论坛关键人物“Toha”，他自2005年起涉足网络犯罪，曾创办Hack-All论坛，后更名为exploit[.]in，并于2018年出售。Toha还被认为与DaMaGeLaB论坛及多个勒索软件组织如REvil、LockBit、Conti和Qiliin有关。尽管欧洲刑警未公布具体身份，但有线索指向一名叫Anton Medvedovskiy或Anton Avdeev的男子。论坛在暗网重新上线，但成员对被捕者身份未达成共识。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对网络犯罪、身份追踪及相关事件的讨论

不同观点：
• Noumenon72 对身份追踪链中出现名为 "Honeypo"（蜜罐）的用户表示怀疑，认为这可能存在可疑之处，暗示可能有执法机构参与设套。
• oezi 质疑为什么成功的网络犯罪分子会选择生活在欧洲，而不是那些欧洲刑警组织和FBI等机构无法触及的地方。他隐含的观点是，网络犯罪分子通常会选择更安全的避风港，而非自投罗网。
• Hilift 引用了一个具体事件：一名38岁的俄罗斯犯罪团伙头目在乌克兰基辅被捕，并提到这导致俄罗斯网络犯罪论坛出现混乱。Hilift 进一步猜测这种混乱可能与支付问题或资金池耗尽有关。
• brcmthrowaway 对 Krebs（可能是指网络安全记者Brian Krebs）敢于曝光俄罗斯论坛中的不法分子表示钦佩，同时暗示这些论坛中的人多为地下室居住的怪胎和失意者。
• vaylian 对报道中使用的术语提出质疑，认为在欧洲刑警组织宣布后，XSS论坛在深网中重新出现，应该使用“暗网”（dark web）而不是“深网”（deep web）来描述该网络环境。

44810945.article_content:
On July 22, 2025, the European police agency
Europol
said
a long-running investigation led by the French Police resulted in the arrest of a 38-year-old administrator of
XSS,
a Russian-language cybercrime forum with more than 50,000 members. The action has triggered an ongoing frenzy of speculation and panic among XSS denizens about the identity of the unnamed suspect, but the consensus is that he is a pivotal figure in the crime forum scene who goes by the hacker handle “
Toha
.” Here’s a deep dive on what’s knowable about Toha, and a short stab at who got nabbed.
An unnamed 38-year-old man was arrested in Kiev last month on suspicion of administering the cybercrime forum XSS. Image: ssu.gov.ua.
Europol did not name the accused, but published partially obscured photos of him from the raid on his residence in Kiev. The police agency said the suspect acted as a trusted third party — arbitrating disputes between criminals — and guaranteeing the security of transactions on XSS. A
statement
from Ukraine’s
SBU
security service said XSS counted among its members many cybercriminals from various ransomware groups, including
REvil
,
LockBit
,
Conti
, and
Qiliin
.
Since the Europol announcement, the XSS forum resurfaced at a new address on the deep web (reachable only via the anonymity network
Tor
). But from reviewing the recent posts, there appears to be little consensus among longtime members about the identity of the now-detained XSS administrator.
The most frequent comment regarding the arrest was a message of solidarity and support for Toha, the handle chosen by the longtime administrator of XSS and several other major Russian forums. Toha’s accounts on other forums have been silent since the raid.
Europol said the suspect has enjoyed a nearly 20-year career in cybercrime, which roughly lines up with Toha’s history. In 2005, Toha was a founding member of the Russian-speaking forum
Hack-All.
That is, until it got massively hacked a few months after its debut. In 2006, Toha rebranded the forum to
exploit[.]in
, which would go on to draw tens of thousands of members, including an eventual Who’s-Who of wanted cybercriminals.
Toha announced in 2018 that he was selling the Exploit forum, prompting rampant speculation on the forums that the buyer was secretly a Russian or Ukrainian government entity or front person. However, those suspicions were unsupported by evidence, and Toha vehemently denied the forum had been given over to authorities.
One of the oldest Russian-language cybercrime forums was
DaMaGeLaB
, which operated from 2004 to 2017, when its administrator “Ar3s” was arrested. In 2018, a partial backup of the DaMaGeLaB forum was
reincarnated as xss[.]is
, with Toha as its stated administrator.
CROSS-SITE GRIFTING
Clues about Toha’s early presence on the Internet — from ~2004 to 2010 — are available in the archives of
Intel 471
, a cyber intelligence firm that tracks forum activity. Intel 471 shows Toha used the same email address across multiple forum accounts, including at Exploit,
Antichat
,
Carder[.]su
and
inattack[.]ru.
DomainTools.com
finds Toha’s email address —
toschka2003@yandex.ru
— was used to register at least a dozen domain names — most of them from the mid- to late 2000s. Apart from exploit[.]in and a domain called
ixyq[.]com
, the other domains registered to that email address end in .ua, the top-level domain for Ukraine (e.g. deleted.org[.]ua, lj.com[.]ua, and blogspot.org[.]ua).
A 2008 snapshot of a domain registered to toschka2003@yandex.ru and to Anton Medvedovsky in Kiev. Note the message at the bottom left, “Protected by Exploit,in.” Image: archive.org.
Nearly all of the domains registered to toschka2003@yandex.ru contain the name
Anton Medvedovskiy
in the registration records, except for the aforementioned ixyq[.]com, which is registered to the name
Yuriy Avdeev
in Moscow.
This Avdeev surname came up in a lengthy conversation with
Lockbitsupp
, the leader of the rapacious and destructive ransomware affiliate group
Lockbit
. The conversation took place in February 2024, when Lockbitsupp asked for help identifying Toha’s real-life identity.
In early 2024, the leader of the Lockbit ransomware group — Lockbitsupp — asked for help investigating the identity of the XSS administrator Toha, which he claimed was a Russian man named Anton Avdeev.
Lockbitsupp didn’t share why he wanted Toha’s details, but he maintained that Toha’s real name was
Anton Avdeev
. I declined to help Lockbitsupp in whatever revenge he was planning on Toha, but his question made me curious to look deeper.
It appears Lockbitsupp’s query was based on a now-deleted Twitter post from 2022, when a user by the name “
3xp0rt
” asserted that Toha was a Russian man named
Anton Viktorovich Avdeev
, born October 27, 1983.
Searching the web for Toha’s email address toschka2003@yandex.ru reveals
a 2010 sales thread
on the forum
bmwclub.ru
where a user named Honeypo was selling a 2007 BMW X5. The ad listed the contact person as Anton A

data.title: The mystery of Alice in Wonderland syndrome
data.author: amichail
data.article_summary: Alice in Wonderland syndrome (AIWS) is a rare condition named after Lewis Carroll's famous character, who experienced size changes. People with AIWS, like nine-year-old Josh Firth, suffer from perceptual distortions, such as seeing objects and body parts as enlarged, elongated, or shrinking. They may also experience time distortions and altered hearing, with sounds appearing too slow or too fast. The exact cause of AIWS remains unknown, though it has been linked to migraines, epilepsy, and infections. First described in 1955, the syndrome highlights how the brain interprets the world through sensory signals and past experiences. When perception is disrupted, it can lead to feelings of depersonalization or derealization, making the world seem unreal. Researchers hope studying AIWS will provide insights into how the brain processes reality.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同个体对现实感丧失和人格解体的体验及其可能原因

不同观点：
• ric2z认为自己的现实感丧失和人格解体症状持续了三周，感到极度迷失和恐惧，但精神科医生仅将其归因于焦虑并开具药物，最终症状自行消失，不确定药物是否真正有效。
• dustractor指出，自己的症状常被误诊为恐慌症，但实际上与恐慌无关，更多是由于对规模和空间的感知失常，音乐和歌词帮助他们度过了青少年时期的困扰。
• jameskilton表示，这种症状在成长过程中时有发生，尽管现在能够通过逻辑控制，但童年时的体验非常恐怖，使用一些应对策略如开灯睡觉来缓解恐惧。
• HelloUsername提供了一个可能相关的链接，讨论了与爱丽丝梦游仙境综合症相关的感知异常，将讨论引向了一个已知的医学现象。

44804768.article_content:
The mystery of Alice in Wonderland syndrome
14 March 2023
Share
Save
Roberta Angheleanu
Features correspondent
Share
Save
Getty Images
Alice in Wonderland syndrome is named after the character dreamed up by author Lewis Carroll, who may have also suffered from the condition (Credit: Getty Images)
A surprising number of people experience symptoms of this curious condition, which is named after Lewis Carroll's heroine, who changed size after eating and drinking
Nine-year-old Josh Firth was in the car with his parents when he noticed something strange happening to the buildings on either side – they seemed to be getting bigger. When he told his mother, Sonja, she was baffled. As far as she was concerned, the buildings looked the same as they always had. "As the car was moving, the buildings on either side suddenly became enlarged and felt as if they were closing down on him," says Sonja.
It wasn't the only time this would happen. After returning from school one day, Josh, who is from Canberra, Australia, told his mother how "his teachers' faces became bigger, out of proportion to their bodies and the walls of the schoolroom got elongated and further away from him". Josh says that on one occasion when playing chess at school, he noticed "his fingers getting wider and bigger to the point of feeling unable to pick up the chess pieces".
These bizarre episodes were most frightening at night, when "the edges of his room were changing, the walls becoming wonky and closing down on him", leading to night terrors, according to Sonja. She says that, at times, her son would say her voice sounds different and he experiences her speech at a "lower pitch and a slower rate".
It took nearly two years for the family to find out what was going on. Josh suffers from a rare disorder known as Alice In Wonderland syndrome, sometimes also called Todd's syndrome.
Alice in Wonderland syndrome (AIWS) affects the way people perceive the world around them and can distort how they
experience their own bodies and the space it occupies
. These can include distortions in vision as well as time. Imagine
seeing people's faces change into dragon-like faces
all your life. This symptom is
only one of the 40 types of visual distortions characteristic of Alice in Wonderland syndrome.
Some patients also describe seeing different
body parts added to the people in front of them
, such as a shortened arm attached to the face of the person sitting in front of them. Other symptoms include
seeing people or objects moving in slow motion or moving unnaturally fast
or not at all.
Their hearing can also be affected – sufferers can hear loved ones
speaking oddly slow
or
unnaturally fast
. And they report seeing
objects or their own body parts shrinking or swelling in front of their eyes, creating
the sensation that they are themselves changing size, just as Josh experienced.
It is this last symptom that led to the disorder's name, after Lewis Carroll's fictional character, who shrinks after drinking a potion and then grows after eating cake. Carroll himself may have even been inspired by perceptual distortions himself, perhaps
brought on by migraine
auras – temporary
visual disturbances that often occur in migraine
sufferers. Others have suggested the author could have suffered from
Alice in Wonderland Syndrome that was triggered by epilepsy,
substance misuse or even an infection.
(
Read more about
the messages hidden within Alice in Wonderland
.
)
Despite being formally described by doctors as a distinct syndrome in 1955 and some symptoms being recorded by doctors even earlier than this, the exact causes of Alice in Wonderland syndrome still remain shrouded in a mystery that Alice herself might have found curiouser and curiouser.
As researchers attempt to unravel this strange condition, they hope it could provide vital insights into how our brains interpret the world around us.
Sonja Firth
Thanks to the signals from our assorted senses, which combine with our past life experiences, each of us perceives the world differently to one another. We all exist in our own unique reality. "Perception is not a passive process of merely seeing, hearing, feeling, tasting or smelling," says Moheb Costandi, a London-based neuroscientist and writer who discusses
Alice in Wonderland syndrome in his book Body Am I
. "It is an active process. The brain acts upon incoming sensory stimuli, based on our past experiences and biases. The way we perceive things influences how we act, and how we act influences what we perceive."

44804768.article_summary: Alice in Wonderland syndrome (AIWS) is a rare condition named after Lewis Carroll's famous character, who experienced size changes. People with AIWS, like nine-year-old Josh Firth, suffer from perceptual distortions, such as seeing objects and body parts as enlarged, elongated, or shrinking. They may also experience time distortions and altered hearing, with sounds appearing too slow or too fast. The exact cause of AIWS remains unknown, though it has been linked to migraines, epilepsy, and infections. First described in 1955, the syndrome highlights how the brain interprets the world through sensory signals and past experiences. When perception is disrupted, it can lead to feelings of depersonalization or derealization, making the world seem unreal. Researchers hope studying AIWS will provide insights into how the brain processes reality.

data.title: A Simple CPU on the Game of Life (2021)
data.author: jxmorris12
data.article_summary: 本文是系列文章的第四部分，介绍如何在《生命游戏》中构建数字逻辑门并最终构建一个简单的CPU。这次的目标是创建一个（两级流水线的）无限寄存器机（URM）。URM是一种图灵完备的简单计算机模型，仅有三个基本操作：递增（INC）、递减（DEC）和条件跳转（JNZ）。尽管这些操作看似简单，但它们足以实现任何计算任务。本文详细描述了如何设计CPU的各个组件，包括时钟、寄存器文件、算术逻辑单元（ALU）、程序计数器和只读存储器（ROM）。与传统CPU设计不同，在《生命游戏》中构建CPU需要考虑特殊的效率标准，重点在于电路的深度和同步性，而不仅仅是减少晶体管数量。最终，作者展示了一个可以在《生命游戏》中执行因数分解程序的实际计算机。

A Simple CPU on the Game of Life - Part 4
by
Nicholas Carlini
2021-12-30
This is the fourth article in a series of posts that I've been making
on creating digital logic gates in the game of life. The
first
,
couple
of
articles
started out with how to create digital logic gates and use them in
order to construct simple circuits.
In this post we're going to actually build a first real computer:
a (2-stage pipelined) unlimited register machine.
And later on
(
[5]
)
we'll make an even better computer.
Pictured below is the execution of an unlimited register machine which is
running a program that factors the number 15 it does this in just a few minutes.
You might think that this is a simple task, but let me just remind you
that it was only a few years ago that quantum computers managed this impressive
feat.
Background
At this point I'm not going to explain what
Conway's game of life
is, or I use it to build circuits that run on the game of life.
I've done that
three
times
before
and these backgrounds get boring to write.
Fortunately for you,
even though this is the fourth time I'm writing about this, in practice you
only need to read the
last post
to get caught up enough for this one to make sense.
CPU Overview
Before you can reasonably understand why I'm making the desgn decisions I am,
I finally have to tell you what a URM actually is.
First described
as a mathematical formaliziation of what is computable,
a URM is a Turing complete, four-instruction CPU that should (in theory) have an unlimited numver
of registers, each of which can hold unbounded integers. Because we're dealing
with the real world, our CPU is going to allow just 16 registers, each of which
will be able to hold four bits.
An unlimited register machine can do only three operations on the registers:
Increment
(INC Rx) a target register by one.
Decrement
(DEC Rx) a target register by one.
Jump
(JNZ Rx, Addr) to a target instruction if the current register is nonzero.
Now these three simple operations don't seem like much, but it turns out they're
actually Turing complete. Which is kind of amazing.
To see this let's first observe that we can use these primitives to emulate some
other common instructions
ZERO
(ZRO Rx) a target register by continuously decrementing the register
as long as it's not zero: DEC Rx; JMP Rx, -1.
Unconditionally jump
(JMP Addr) to a target instruction by reserving a
temporary register Ry that is always positive, and running (JNZ Ry, Addr).
So, for example, if we wanted to add the contents of Register 1 to the contents of
Register 2 you might implement something like
ADD:
jnz R1, END
dec R1
inc R2
jmp ADD
END:
which will result in R2 now containing R1+R2 (and zeros R1 in the process).
With that out of the way, behold, a CPU that implements this:
The overall layout of our computer is going to be entirely standard.
In the upper left corner we have our
clock
, which works exactly
as described
last time
. This is going to
keep everything synchronized so we run each instruction one by one.
To the right of the clock is the register file, which holds 16 four-bit registers
using the D-flip-flops that we developed last time.
This is the entirety of the RAM of this machine---64 bits.
To the right of the register file is a little tiny Arithmetic Logic Unit (the ALU),
which computes the actual mathematical functions the CPU supports.
Because this is a URM, it can only increment.
And below the register file is another series of
D-flip-flops this time storing the program counter, which
is what holds the current instruction we're executing.
Below the program counter is the ROM which holds the program text that we're
going to execute. This ROM can hold up to 128 different (four-bit) instructions.
To the left of the program ROM is another collection of the
flip-flops.
These flip-flops actually allow this CPU to have a two-stage
pipeline that can both fetch and execute instructions simultaneously.
Finally at right is the output of the computer in the form of four 7-segment displays.
These are almost exactly the same seventh segment displays that I built in the last post.
Efficient Circuit Design Criteria
The basic construction of a CPU is actually relatively simple, and we really
only need to do just a few things to turn a collection of digital logic gates
into a full computer.
Now because this is an article that's meant to focus on designing the game
of life computer and not on computers generally I don't want to spend (much) on the
generic bits that would let you design a computer with normal logic gates.
Other people have done that.
Instead what I want to focus on is what changes when you're building a CPU
on top of the game of life.
Let's start with the key difference.
When building real computers, the ultimate design criteria is to try and
minimize (something like) the number of total transistors that are used (or,
more accurately, the depth of the circuit, but let's not get pedantic).
The reason

data.title: Ch.at – A lightweight LLM chat service accessible through HTTP, SSH, DNS and API
data.author: ownlife
data.article_summary: "ch.at" 是一个提供多种智能聊天服务的平台，读作 "ch-dot-at"。它支持通过不同方式进行交互，包括传统聊天、SSH访问、使用curl命令查询以及通过dig命令获取文本信息。该平台不保留日志、无需账户注册，并且其软件是开源免费的。用户可以通过GitHub获取相关软件资源。平台强调隐私保护和灵活的访问方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕网站ch.at及其相关技术实现、可持续性、隐私和实用性的讨论

不同观点：
• 第一种观点：作者（etaioinshrdlu）解释了创建ch.at网站的初衷，强调了其无JS设计、短域名的创意、使用GPT4o模型的理由，并提到未来可能引入更多LLM模型的计划。作者还分享了项目背后的技术灵感和运营成本情况。（支持项目的创新性和技术实现）

• 第二种观点：Zaik指出项目未实现IRC、XMPP和SIP等聊天协议，质疑这些协议为何被忽略。（对技术实现的质疑）

• 第三种观点：FraserGreenlee对使用GPT4o模型的可持续性提出疑问，建议参考RNN模型或HuggingFace的Gradio Spaces，提出对更开放和可持续的LLM平台的兴趣。（对技术选型和可持续性的关注）

• 第四种观点：Puppymaster分享了在飞机上使用该服务的实际体验，认为其适合进行轻量阅读和学习 obscure 主题。（支持项目的实用性）

• 第五种观点：Dakinitribe表示该工具帮助其快速集成脚本，提升了工作效率，并对项目的整体设计表示赞赏。（支持项目的功能和效率）

• 第六种观点：Userbinator用类比“apples, oranges, pears, and fruits”质疑“and API”的合理性。（对技术术语使用的质疑）

• 第七种观点：Indigodaddy关注项目如何应对请求过载或DDoS攻击的问题，担心服务的可持续性。（对服务稳定性和安全性的关注）

• 第八种观点：HiPHInch建议将“dig @ch.at TXT +short”命令别名为‘c’，以便快速使用。（对用户体验的改进建议）

• 第九种观点：WhatsName对两字母域名的稀有性和价值表示惊讶。（对域名价值的讨论）

• 第十种观点：Tamimio提到其提问的5个问题中，有4个因“无法访问实时数据”而未能得到回答，质疑服务的实际能力。（对服务功能和数据访问的质疑）

补充讨论：
• 一些用户（如3s）对如何在飞机上不付费使用LLM服务表示关注，并欣赏项目的隐私保护设计。（对项目实用性和隐私保护的支持）

• Indigodaddy再次表达了对项目及其未来潜力的积极看法，认为这样的工具能激发AI/LLM领域的积极发展。（对项目整体的乐观态度）

• Alhirzel对项目的经济性提出了疑问，关注其运营成本和经济模型。（对项目经济可行性的关注）

争议焦点：
• 项目的技术实现是否完善，如是否应支持IRC、XMPP和SIP等协议。
• 使用GPT4o模型的可持续性以及是否应探索其他更开放和可持续的模型。
• 服务在面对大量请求时的稳定性和安全性如何保障。

data.title: Abusing Entra OAuth for fun and access to internal Microsoft applications
data.author: the1bernard
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者如何意外获取微软内部22个服务的访问权限。作者在写文档时，注意到微软的短链接服务aka.ms，并好奇访问其主页，发现一个登录界面。经过多次尝试，作者通过一个多租户配置错误的工程中心应用，成功访问了微软内部工程门户，查看到大量敏感信息。该问题源于Entra ID在多租户应用中的认证和授权处理不当，导致外部用户可通过同意提示获取内部访问权限。作者随后向微软安全响应中心报告了该问题，并探讨了其他可能受影响的微软服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：微软Entra ID及相关安全问题，特别是文档和授权机制的复杂性与漏洞。

不同观点：
• **微软文档混乱，难以使用**：  
  - Contortion和Too认为微软的文档难以理解，缺乏有效的入门指南，且充斥着不实用的链接和术语，导致用户在配置时如"瞎子摸象"。
  - yyyk进一步指出，Entra ID应仅用于认证(AuthN)，授权(AuthZ)应自行处理，避免复杂性。

  - victor106认为Azure和Entra ID过于复杂，建议使用Okta，尽管价格更高，但文档更完善，安全性更好。

Home
Consent & Compromise: Abusing Entra OAuth for Fun and Access to Internal Microsoft Applications
← Return to overview
Consent & Compromise: Abusing Entra OAuth for Fun and Access to Internal Microsoft Applications
Aug 7, 2025
By:
Vaisha Bernard
This blog is about how I got access to over 22 internal Microsoft services and how you might be vulnerable too.
After my
last talk at the 38C3 conference in Hamburg
, this was the top comment on YouTube.
Well, this story definitely falls in the category “someone stumbling around finding horrifying vulnerabilities”. Although this time I was not even having issues, I was just distracted from a boring task.
You see, I was writing some documentation the other day, when my Eye fell on one of those aka.ms links. For those of you who don’t know, aka.ms is the
URL shortener service used by Microsoft
.
My mind started to wonder. Where would you end up if you would just visit
https://aka.ms
, so without any shortener link included?
A login screen. This is probably where Microsoft employees manage their links. I did wonder though, what would happen if I simply tried logging in here myself with my own Microsoft account? Surely, that would not work, right?
Of course not! You need an account in the Microsoft tenant, otherwise, no luck. Back to writing that boring documentation. But what was that?
An indexing service for aka.ms links
? Interesting.
And one of those links points to an eng.ms domain. What is that?
Another login screen! It did not work the first time, but maybe I can login here! The result surprised me.
I got a consent prompt, asking me to give consent to share my basic profile information with this application. Sure, why not? Does that mean this is an application I can access?
After clicking “accept”, I get a 500 Internal Server Error message. I’m pretty sure that was this server trying to tell me that this application was not meant to be accessed by me. But now I’m intrigued, what is eng.ms? I still had that documentation to write, but that had to wait.
I started subdomain enumeration on the domain eng.ms and found an interesting subdomain: rescue.eng.ms. This gave me another login screen and another consent prompt. But this time it gave me access using my own Microsoft 365 account! Notice my name in the upper right corner?
I quickly realized that I should not have access here. This Engineering Hub was some sort of portal for Microsoft Engineers. I must admit, my knee-jerk reaction as a red-teamer was to search for the phrase “password”. What can I say, I could not help myself. It returned 13,252 hits, all referring to internal Microsoft procedures and product groups. I was clearly not supposed to access this.
I stopped here and reported this to the Microsoft Security Response Centre (MSRC). But what had happened here? Why was I able to access this internal portal and might other services be vulnerable in the same way?
To answer that question, we need to have a closer look at how Entra ID handles authentication and authorization for multi-tenant applications.
Multi-Tenant Applications
When developers want to use Entra for authentication to a web application, the application needs to first be registered at Entra. This is called an “App Registration” or “Application Object”. These applications can be set to accept users from the tenant where they are registered (single-tenant), or users from any tenant (multi-tenant). They can also be configured to accept “personal Microsoft accounts”.
App developers are then tasked to configure the authorization server (login.microsoftonline.com in most cases) in application logic and all four options above have a corresponding desired value for the authorization server URL.
So single-tenant applications should be configured to use
https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenantid>
or
https://login.microsoftonline.com/<domain>
as the authorization server, while multi-tenant applications that also accept personal Microsoft accounts should use
https://login.microsoftonline.com/common
.
The Engineering Hub was configured as a multi-tenant application and redirected me to the /common endpoint.
This allowed me to login (step 1 & 2) with my own “work or school account”, which triggered a Consent prompt (Step 3), as the application was not used in my own tenant before. When I gave it consent, it was instantiated into a Service Principal or “Enterprise Application” (step 4) in my own tenant and returned an access token (step 5).
This access token was issued by my own tenant. The “iss” (issuer) and “tid” (tenant ID) claims were set to values corresponding with my own tenant. Any conditional access policies or user assignment took place in my own tenant according to my own configuration. I was authenticated & authorized, only by the wrong authority. And nowhere in application logic was this checked.
This made me wonder. What other Microsoft services could be impacted by this misconfiguration? Let’s find out!
Mapping the Microsoft Attack Surface

data.title: Don't “let it crash”, let it heal
data.author: ahamez
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了Elixir编程中"let it crash"这一常见理念的误解和问题。作者指出，虽然BEAM虚拟机允许进程崩溃后自动重启，但这一理念常被错误理解为可忽视所有错误处理。实际上，盲目应用这一理念会导致糟糕的用户体验（如频繁重置连接）和无法向用户反馈错误信息。作者建议采取折中方案：对不可恢复的异常情况允许崩溃，但对可预见的错误应进行适当处理并向用户提供有用反馈，而非简单地让进程崩溃重启。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Elixir/Erlang中的"let it crash"哲学及其在构建可靠系统中的应用

不同观点：
• **强调Joe Armstrong博士论文的重要性**：hesus_ruiz认为解释"let it crash"概念时应提及Joe Armstrong的博士论文，这是理解可靠分布式系统的关键文献。
• **错误处理的阶段性改进**：valenterry提出了错误处理的四个阶段，从运行时检测崩溃到编译时检测潜在崩溃，并认为文章中描述的哲学仅停留在第一阶段，有待改进。
• **"Let it heal"的讨论**：goosejuice和stcg讨论了"Let it heal"这一表述，认为其不如"Let it crash"引人注目，但更贴近Joe Armstrong的思想。
• **"Let it crash"的误解**：tmcb和IshKebab指出，很多人仅从字面上理解"Let it crash"，误以为其意味着忽略错误处理，而实际上这是一种设计系统的策略，确保崩溃不会导致系统灾难性失败。

补充讨论：
• **崩溃后重启的有效性**：HexDecOctBin质疑如果进程因缺少文件而崩溃，重启后问题仍存在，如何通过重启来解决问题。monkeyelite补充说明，这种策略在BEAM中有效，而在其他环境如fast-cgi进程中则无此必要。
• **与Kubernetes等系统的比较**：refactor_master将"let it crash"与Kubernetes中容器崩溃后重启的机制进行比较，认为两者在概念上有相似之处，但应用层次不同。
• **监督树和错误处理**：Jtsummers详细解释了Erlang中监督树的概念，以及其与传统语言中错误处理的差异，强调了BEAM中进程的轻量级特性和监督树的重要性。
• **哲学的进一步阐述**：juped引用了Joe Armstrong论文中的相关内容，进一步阐述了"let it crash"的哲学，强调了在程序遇到无法处理的错误时应崩溃，并由其他进程处理错误。
• **不同系统哲学的比较**：anthk比较了不同系统哲学，如Unix/BSD的"Crash, fix, restart"和GNU/MIT/Lisp的"Detect, offer a fix, continue"。
• **"Reset on error"的建议**：adastra22建议用"Reset on error"来替代"Let it crash"，认为这种表述更能准确传达该哲学的核心思想。

争议焦点：
• **"Let it crash"是否意味着忽略错误处理**：一些人认为该哲学意味着忽略错误处理，而实际上其强调的是设计一个能够容错和自愈的系统。
• **该哲学的适用范围和有效性**：讨论了在不同环境和系统中该策略的适用性和有效性，包括与Kubernetes等系统的比较。

总结：评论中对"let it crash"哲学的理解存在多种观点，主要集中在对其误解、适用范围、与其他系统的比较以及更准确的表述等方面。

This is the first of a series on misconceptions about Elixir. These are my opinions. I hope they spark discussion and that maybe we all learn things as a result.
A note to the Elixir programmers who commonly say “let it crash”: This phrase gives outsiders and newcomers the wrong idea, and encourages bad habits for those who misinterpret it. If I had my way, we would stop saying it.
Let it crash.
Elixir runs on the BEAM VM. If you’re familiar, skip to the next paragraph. Otherwise, some necessary context is that on the BEAM, all code is executed in a “process”. This can be thought of kind of like a green thread. Each process is a lightweight, share-nothing unit of concurrency. Processes communicate via message passing. When processes encounter an unhandled error, the process exits. We use supervisors (which are themselves supervised typically), to then restart any given crashed process.
When people say “let it crash”, they are referring to the fact that practically any exited process in your application will be subsequently restarted. Because of this, you can often be much less defensive around unexpected errors. You will see far fewer try/rescue, or matching on error states in Elixir code.
The “it” in “let it crash” to an Elixir programmer is
a process.
Not your application.
In practice, an Elixir application almost
never
crashes, even in conditions that would hard-quit in any other system.
For those without the context of building Elixir applications, “let it crash” gives the impression of “jank”, of non-elegant code that does not consider user experience or possible failure states. A panic or crash in most languages is a catastrophic event, to be avoided at all costs.
Even for Elixir developers with experience, “let it crash” as a practice loses enough nuance so as to be reductive, and I’ve seen it actively impact the quality of code that comes across my desk.
First, we’ll talk about why you shouldn’t “let it crash”, and then we’ll talk about what you should do instead.
Processes are tied to real things
Open a socket connection, receiving or sending an HTTP request, opening a file, connecting to a database: all of these things are typically backed by a process. 99% of the time, that process is linked to the process that asked for that to happen. The most straightforward example of this is in the context of a web server communicating over a web socket, and if you’re familiar with it, Phoenix LiveView.
Lets imagine that we embrace the “let it crash” philosophy to the bone, and we write some code like this, handling a web socket message:
This code will crash the process in the following scenarios:
the pattern match on the event name fails `”import_data”`
the pattern match on the input params fails (there is no “data” key)
`data` is not a list (technically, an enumerable of some kind)
Any given item in data fails to be created or raises an error
In some cases, especially “invalid messages that should not be producible”, crashing is a
good
thing. For the first two, and maybe three things in the list above, hitting those cases implies a bug in your front end likely. Someone sending your process messages it was never designed to handle. Crashing may be the desired behavior.
BUT:
There is a user on the other end of this. In the case of LiveView, the web socket is driving at least some part of their experience. Establishing a websocket takes time. What will the user experience be? Will they see a flash message about something going wrong? Will some of their UI state reset? None of these things are really acceptable. This pattern is all over, not just tied to LiveView. Do you want to close whatever file/database connection you have every time anything goes wrong? Or release some other expensive resource? What if you encounter thousands errors in quick succession? Will restarting be expensive?
Representing Failed States
Intentionally crashing on any possible error also means that you are not
able to represent errored states to your users
. For our above example, something like this might make more sense:
In this example, instead of just crashing and seeing some generic error, the user is given actionable information about what went wrong. We have represented the failed state.
With that said, in practice we take a middle-way. Specifically, in fully unexpected scenarios that cannot be remediated, like getting a malformed “import_data” command, it is often
preferable
to crash. We crash because the process is now in an unrecoverable bad state, and we don’t know how it got there. In this case, we want to remount the component into a good state. You still have to consider the UX of this scenario, and design your pages to gracefully remount.
