• **starchild3001**：认为gpt-oss的创新主要在于对已知优化技术的巧妙组合，而非激进的架构变革。特别提到MXFP4量化技术使得模型能够在消费级显卡上运行，这对独立开发者和研究人员非常有帮助。同时提出未来可能会出现“推理模型”与“知识库模型”的分离。
• **7moritz7**：对Qwen3在本地的表现更为认可，认为其在遵循提示和自然性方面优于gpt-oss。同时指出gpt-oss在逻辑推理能力上表现不佳。
• **mark_l_watson**：赞赏Sebastian Raschka的博客，分享了自己使用get-oss和Qwen3模型的经验，并表达了对过去能够自己实现简单LLM的怀念。
• **roscas**：基于个人经验，认为Qwen3在代码处理上表现更好，速度快且输出优秀，而gpt-oss则显得缓慢。
• **eurekin**：对Qwen3 coder在本地运行的高效性和实用性表示赞赏，认为其已经具备实际应用价值。
• **gglon**：引用混合模型的例子，指出在现代开源LLM架构趋同的情况下，训练方法（数据、RL等）成为创新的主要领域。
• **poorman**：明确推荐使用Qwen3-coder，认为其工具调用能力远胜gpt-oss。

补充讨论：
• **Scene_Cast2**：指出大多数创新发生在训练（数据、RL）方面，而非架构调整，与传统ML领域的经验相悖。
• **chaos_emergent**：对文章中关于LLM训练通常只进行单轮的陈述提出质疑，认为该说法缺乏证据支持。
• **storus**：在测试中发现gpt-oss在解决研究生级别数学问题时，速度快且所需的思考标记少，表现接近更大规模的模型。
• **ahmedfromtunis**：报告访问某些网站时遇到连接和HSTS相关的问题，属于技术问题反馈。
• **oezi**：提出关于开源模型通过额外训练可能获得的性能提升的疑问。
• **pryelluw**：认为Qwen3的本地使用效果好，虽然不完全信任其输出，但显著改善了网络搜索的精准度。
• **homarp**：提到从GPT-2到gpt-oss的架构进步及其与Qwen3的对比，但没有详细展开。

争议焦点：
• 对gpt-oss与Qwen3在性能、速度和工具调用能力上的对比存在不同看法，尤其是两者在本地运行时的表现。
• 关于LLM训练通常只进行单轮的陈述的真实性存在质疑。

总结：讨论主要围绕gpt-oss和Qwen3的架构、性能和实用性展开，不同用户基于个人经验对两者的优劣有不同看法，且对未来模型开发方向提出了各自见解。

data.title: AOL closes its dial up internet service
data.author: simonjgreen
data.article_summary: AOL宣布将于2025年9月30日关闭其拨号上网服务，该服务已运行34年。尽管大多数人早已不再使用拨号上网，AOL仍正式结束了其Dial-up Internet服务及相关软件AOL Dialer和AOL Shield浏览器的支持。其电子邮件服务将继续运营。文章回顾了AOL作为早期互联网服务提供商的历史，尤其是在英国市场的发展，包括1990年代的拨号上网服务及之后被Carphone Warehouse收购并重塑为TalkTalk的历程。AOL英国分支多年前已停止接收新客户，此次关闭主要影响北美地区。文章还提及AOL曾通过限制性软件提供上网服务，但很快被宽带和有线网络超越。最终，拨号上网技术因过时而彻底退出历史舞台。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AOL拨号服务的结束及其影响

不同观点：
• MalbertKerman提到AOL服务的结束时间，带有些许讽刺意味，可能认为该服务早就应该结束。
• mrandish对过去技术的回忆充满怀旧，提到早期v.56调制解调器的出现和其带来的速度感。
• seydor开玩笑地认为拨号调制解调器的声音可能像黑胶唱机一样重新流行起来。
• DarkFuture描述了在1998/1999年英国使用拨号上网的痛苦经历，尤其是在有限的上网时间内的期待和焦虑。
• mtillman提供了一个链接，表示仍有类似服务存在，减轻了人们对拨号服务消失的担忧。
• empleton质疑AOL服务在宽带时代仍然存在的原因，怀疑是用户未主动取消或未意识到不再需要该服务。
• naz对AOL拨号在英国的使用体验非常不满，特别是由于流量路由导致的高延迟问题。
• didip关注AOL服务关闭对员工就业的影响，担心裁员问题。
• umanwizard对AOL拨号服务在2025年仍然存在感到惊讶，暗示其早已过时。
• MiddleEndian对AOL的评价褒贬不一，批评其对浏览器和关键词的强制使用，但赞赏AOL Instant Messenger的功能和便利性。
• austinallegro以幽默的方式告别AOL拨号，提到免费试用CD的普遍存在和其带来的安慰。
• edm0nd和SeanAnderson简单表达了对AOL拨号服务结束的感慨。
• cwmoore以幽默方式描述了看到新闻标题时联想到的调制解调器连接音，挑战AI的反应。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次出现怀旧和对过去技术的怀念，如mrandish和austinallegro对早期调制解调器和免费CD的回忆。
• 对AOL服务的技术问题和用户体验有较多讨论，特别是naz提到的高延迟问题和MiddleEndian对AOL浏览器及关键词的批评。
• 评论中还有对拨号服务关闭后影响的关注，如didip对员工失业的担忧。
• 争议焦点可能在于AOL服务在宽带时代仍然存在的原因，以及其对早期互联网发展的正面和负面影响。

After 34 Years AOL Finally Closes its Dial-up Internet Service
Sunday, Aug 10th, 2025 (7:44 am) - Score 4,520
Email
|
Link News
15 Comments
In a somewhat surprising development, mainly because almost everybody assumed it had died a long time ago,
AOL
(America Online) – one of the very first consumer ISPs in both the USA and UK – recently caused a stir again by announcing that it had “
decided to discontinue Dial-up Internet
” on 30th September 2025.
According to
AOL’s website
: “
AOL routinely evaluates its products and services and has decided to discontinue Dial-up Internet. This service will no longer be available in AOL plans. As a result, on September 30, 2025 this service and the associated software, the AOL Dialer software and AOL Shield browser, which are optimized for older operating systems and dial-up internet connections, will be discontinued
.” But their email service will continue.
NOTE:
Many
dialup
ISPs in the UK during 1995 – like AOL – used expensive premium rate numbers, although this did soon gravitate to local call rates and then unmetered via FRIACO. The v90
dialup
standard (56Kbps capable or 0.056Mbps) didn’t arrive until 1998 and by then
ADSL
and cable broadband were just around the corner – ready to revolutionise the market.
The change appears to have been announced within the past few weeks, although it wasn’t picked up more widely until journalist
Ernie Smith
noted it in a post on
Bluesky
. Just to be clear, the announcement above refers to the USA and Canada. However, we’re fairly confident that what remains of AOL UK (aka –
TalkTalk
) doesn’t have any legacy dial-up customers left, although we would have said the same about the USA and Canada too, until that announcement dropped (dial-up speeds in 2025 would be practically unusable). ISPreview is currently checking, just to be sure.
Advertisement
In case anybody has forgotten. The original AOL UK experience was somewhat of a walled-garden way of accessing the internet, which forced you to use the company’s own software and restricted your ability to access certain internet services. This had the benefit of simplifying the experience, but AOL later fell behind the curve and ended up being overtaken by rivals.
The
Carphone Warehouse
(CPW) ultimately won the auction to buy AOL UK’s Internet access business in 2006 for £370m (note: AOL’s content division became a separate business). At the time, AOL were the UK’s third-largest ISP with around
2.1 million customers
(600,000 on dial-up and 1.5 million with broadband) and were later re-branded to AOL Broadband.
A second big change occurred on 29th March 2010, when CPW and
TalkTalk
separated (demerged) – the latter became a separate business, which included customers from CPW’s prior acquisitions (e.g. AOL Broadband, Tiscali etc.). Several more years passed until May 2014, when TalkTalk confirmed that AOL Broadband (formerly AOL UK) had stopped taking on new internet and phone customers (
here
), although no mention was made of the dial-up base.
We’re certain that plenty of our readers (those now of a certain age group) will have stories to share of the early AOL UK days. Yours truly only used the original service briefly, before promptly switching away as the UK’s then dialup (narrowband) internet market became more competitive, affordable and less restrictive. It’s a service I was glad to forget, but it played an important role.

data.title: Flintlock – Create and manage the lifecycle of MicroVMs, backed by containerd
data.author: Palmik
data.article_summary: Flintlock 是一个用于创建和管理微虚拟机（MicroVMs）生命周期的服务，支持 Cloud Hypervisor 和 Firecracker 虚拟机监控器（VMMs）。它最初由 Weaveworks 开发，现由社区维护，是 Liquid Metal 项目的一部分，可通过 Cluster API Provider Microvm 进行编排。Flintlock 通过 gRPC 或 HTTP API 实现微虚拟机的创建、删除和生命周期管理，支持使用 OCI 镜像和 cloud-init 等配置元数据，并即将支持 CNI 网络配置。此外，它还提供 Prometheus 指标收集功能。项目文档提供了入门教程和贡献指南，兼容多个版本的 Firecracker 和 Cloud Hypervisor，采用 MPL-2.0 许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕"Backed by containerd"及相关技术（如Cloud Hypervisor、容器与虚拟机技术）的困惑与看法

不同观点：
• [rzzzt] 认为文档中对"Backed by containerd"的解释不够清晰，直到查阅文档后才明白其作用（例如用于拉取镜像，但并不作为容器运行时）。这表明对技术细节的了解需要依赖额外的文档支持。
• [ofrzeta] 表示首次听说"Cloud Hypervisor"，并指出在当前技术快速发展的背景下，跟上所有新技术的步伐变得非常困难。这反映了一些技术人员面对技术更新迭代的压力。
• [dboreham] 认为这些新技术（容器作为虚拟机）的概念很好，但在实际使用中往往非常麻烦，不如Docker那样易于使用。因此，在达到Docker那样的易用性之前，这些技术难以成为主流。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于新技术的实用性和易用性。尽管新技术可能在理论上具有优势，但实际应用中的复杂性限制了其广泛普及。[dboreham] 的观点特别指出了与Docker对比下的使用体验问题，这是技术社区中常见的讨论点。
• [ofrzeta] 的评论还揭示了技术社区中存在对新技术信息过载的担忧，这可能影响开发者对新工具的接受度。

Flintlock - Create and manage the lifecycle of MicroVMs, backed by containerd.
What is flintlock?
🎉
This project was originally developed by Weaveworks but is now owned & run by the community. If you are interested in helping out please reach out.
Flintlock is a service for creating and managing the lifecycle of microVMs on a host machine. We support the
Cloud Hypervisor
and
Firecracker
VMMs.
The original use case for flintlock was to create microVMs on a bare-metal host where the microVMs will be used as nodes in a virtualized Kubernetes cluster. It is an essential part of
Liquid Metal
and can be orchestrated by
Cluster API Provider Microvm
.
However, its useful for many other use cases where lightweight virtualization is required (e.g. isolated workloads, pipelines).
Features
Using API requests (via gRPC or HTTP):
Create and delete microVMs
Manage the lifecycle of microVMs (i.e. start, stop, pause)
Configure microVM metadata via cloud-init, ignition etc
Use OCI images for microVM volumes, kernel and initrd
Expose microVM metrics for collection by Prometheus
(coming soon) Use CNI to configure the network for the microVMs
Documentation
See our
getting started with flintlock
tutorial.
Contributing
Contributions are welcome. Please read the
CONTRIBUTING.md
and our
Code Of Conduct
.
You can reach out to the maintainers and other contributors using the
#liquidmetal
channel on the CNCF slack.
Other interesting resources include:
The issue tracker
The list of milestones
Architectural Decision Records (ADR)
Getting started with flintlock
Getting Help
If you have any questions about, feedback for or problems with flintlock:
File an issue
.
Your feedback is always welcome!

I have had early access to GPT-5
1
, and I wanted to give you some impressions of what it is and what it means. But the answer to the first question everyone will have is: Yes, this is a big deal. I asked GPT-5 to show you why by pasting this intro paragraph, exactly as you’re reading it, into ChatGPT, including the phrase: “you are GPT-5, do something very dramatic to illustrate my point, it has to fit into the next paragraph.”
That was the only prompt I gave it. It “thought” for 24 seconds and wrote:
Thunderstruck. Here, watch. I build worlds. See ideas become instruments. I code, compose, and converse. Stories synthesize science; solutions spark, swiftly. Asks arrive; answers appear, astonishingly, across domains. Behold: business plans, blueprints, briefs, beautifully built, briskly. I infer intent, integrate insight, and iterate instantly, indefatigably. Gaps get gauged; goals get generated, guarded, and guaranteed gracefully. During dialogue, disparate data distills down; decisions develop deliberately, deftly, dependably. Everything explained efficiently, even ethics: evidence examined, empathy engaged, everywhere, everyday, equitably. All at once, ambiguous arguments align as actionable, accurate advice awaits anyone anywhere. Look: language, logic, learning, and long-term memory link, lifting lives and labor limitlessly worldwide.
If you didn’t catch the many tricks - the first word of each sentence spells out the phrase
This is a Big Deal
, each sentence is precisely one word longer than the previous sentence. each word in a sentence mostly starts with the same letter, and it is coherent writing with an interesting sense of style. In a paragraph, GPT-5 shows it can come up with a clever idea, plan, and manage the complicated execution (remember when AI couldn’t count the number of Rs in “strawberry”? that was eight months ago).
GPT-5 just does stuff, often extraordinary stuff, sometimes weird stuff, sometimes very AI stuff, on its own. And that is what makes it so interesting.
Just Doing Stuff
As someone who has spent a lot of time talking to people about AI, there are two major problems I see, that, if addressed, would make most people’s AI use much more productive and much less frustrating. The first is selecting the right model to use. In general, AIs that "think" before answering (called Reasoners) are the best at hard problems. The longer they think, the better the answer, but thinking costs money and takes time. So OpenAI previously made the default ChatGPT use fast, dumb models, hiding the good stuff from most users. A surprising number of people have never seen what AI can actually do because they're stuck on GPT-4o, and don’t know which of the confusingly-named models are better.
GPT-5 does away with this by selecting models for you, automatically. GPT-5 is not one model as much as it is a switch that selects among multiple GPT-5 models of various sizes and abilities. When you ask GPT-5 for something, the AI decides which model to use and how much effort to put into “thinking.” It just does it for you. For most people, this automation will be helpful, and the results might even be shocking, because, having only used default older models, they will get to see what a Reasoner can accomplish on hard problems. But for people who use AI more seriously, there is an issue: GPT-5 is somewhat arbitrary about deciding what a hard problem is.
For example, I asked GPT-5 to “create a svg with code of an otter using a laptop on a plane” (asking for an .svg file requires the AI to blindly draw an image using basic shapes and math, a very hard challenge). Around 2/3 of the time, GPT-5 decides this is an easy problem, and responds instantly, presumably using its weakest model and lowest reasoning time. I get an image like this:
The rest of the time, GPT-5 decides this is a hard problem, and switches to a Reasoner, spending 6 or 7 seconds thinking before producing an image like this, which is much better. How does it choose? I don’t know, but if I ask the model to “think hard” in my prompt, I am more likely to be routed to the better model.
But premium subscribers can directly select the more powerful models, such as the one called (at least for me) GPT-5 Thinking. This removes some of the issues with being at the mercy of GPT-5’s model selector. I found that if I encouraged the model to think hard about the otter, it would spend a good 30 seconds before giving you an images like these the one below - notice the little animations, the steaming coffee cup, and clouds going by outside, none of which I asked for. How to ensure the model puts in the most effort? It is really unclear - GPT-5 just does things for you.
And that ex

data.title: Zig's Lovely Syntax
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 本文简要讨论了Zig语言的语法特点，认为Zig在保持简洁性和可读性方面比Rust更出色。文章首先提到Zig的整数字面量不使用后缀，而是通过编译时推断类型并强制转换，例如`comptime_int`。Zig的字符串字面量支持原始字符串和多行字符串，避免了Rust中复杂的原始字符串语法问题。在记录字面量中，Zig采用类似C的语法，但更注重字段赋值的可搜索性。Zig的类型前缀语法简化了复杂类型的表示，函数声明中去掉了Rust中的箭头符号，使语法更简洁。总体而言，Zig在语法细节上做出了一些优化，提升了代码的可读性和编写体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Zig编程语言的语法设计及其与其他语言（如Rust、C#、Go、D等）的比较，讨论了类型声明、可读性、语法美观性、语法糖（如原始字符串、lambda支持、操作符重载等）以及具体语法使用中的问题和个人偏好。

不同观点：
• **支持Zig语法的观点**：n42认为Zig的语法设计在简洁性、一致性和可读性上达到了很好的平衡，特别是对工业应用场景非常友好。Zig的语法设计虽然不一定在表面上“美观”，但其功能性和一致性值得赞赏。
• **反对Zig语法的观点**：phplovesong和pjmlp对Zig语法中的符号如@和.{ }感到不满，认为这些符号让代码显得杂乱且难以阅读。nromiun也指出，Go语言在不需要使用;和:的情况下也能做得很好，暗示Zig的语法并非最优。
• **对类型声明的不同偏好**：bscphil更喜欢C风格的类型声明，认为Rust等语言的类型声明方式（如`let mut`）增加了不必要的冗长，导致代码可读性下降。他倾向于使用可选的类型推断，只在必要时明确指定类型。
• **对原始字符串语法的讨论**：z_open对Zig的原始字符串语法感到困惑，认为其复杂且不直观。相比之下，kcartlidge更喜欢C# 11的原始字符串语法，认为其处理缩进和嵌入大括号的方式更直观。
• **对lambda支持的需求**：pton_xd和ww520提到Zig缺乏对lambda表达式的支持，这在C++等语言中是常见的特性，且在某些场景（如定义比较器）中非常实用。ww520进一步指出，Zig缺乏链式可选检查和monadic类型支持。
• **对操作符重载的讨论**：the__alchemist对Zig缺乏操作符重载表示遗憾，认为这限制了某些数学类型（如向量、四元数、矩阵）的语法表达能力。

补充讨论：
• **对语法简洁性的进一步探讨**：WalterBright通过对比D语言和Zig的类型声明语法，强调了语法简洁性的重要性。D语言的声明方式更加直接，减少了符号的使用。
• **对可读性和学习曲线的讨论**：Twey和losvedir讨论了语法中单词的音节数对可读性和记忆的影响，暗示更简短的单词可能提高代码的可读性。
• **对复杂语法特性的实现讨论**：MrResearcher提出了Zig中如何实现两个不同的comptime闭包并将其作为函数参数传递的问题，指出了Zig在实现VTable等特性时的复杂性。
• **对语法整体重要性的反思**：hardwaregeek指出，虽然很多人声称“语法不重要”，但实际上语法选择往往隐含了个人偏好，且可能影响语言的普及和接受度。Rust的成功部分归因于其语法设计，这值得其他语言借鉴。

争议焦点：Zig语法的简洁性与美观性、类型声明的可读性、原始字符串的处理方式、lambda支持的必要性以及操作符重载的实用性。

44855881.article_content:
Zig’s Lovely Syntax
Aug 9, 2025
It’s a bit of a silly post, because syntax is the least interesting
detail about the language, but, still, I can’t stop thinking how Zig
gets this detail just right for the class of curly-braced languages,
and, well, now you’ll have to think about that too.
On the first glance, Zig looks almost exactly like Rust, because Zig
borrows from Rust liberally. And I think that Rust has great syntax,
considering all the semantics it needs to express (see
“Rust’s Ugly Syntax”
). But Zig improves on that, mostly by
leveraging simpler language semantics, but also through some purely
syntactical tasteful decisions.
Integer Literals
How do you spell a number ninety-two? Easy,
92
. But
what type is that? Statically-typed languages often come with
several flavors of integers:
u32
,
u64
,
u8
. And there’s often a syntax for literals of a
particular types:
92u8
,
92l
,
92z
.
Zig doesn’t have suffixes, because, in Zig, all integer literals
have the same type:
comptime_int
:
const
an_integer =
92
;
assert(
@TypeOf
(an_integer)
==
comptime_int
);
The value of an integer literal is known at compile time and is
coerced to a specific type on assignment
const x: i32 = 92;
or ascription:
@as(i32, 92)
To emphasize, this is
not
type inference, this is implicit
comptime coercion. This does mean that code like
var x = 92;
generally doesn’t work, and requires an explicit type.
String Literals
Raw or multiline strings are spelled like this:
const
raw =
\\Roses are red
\\  Violets are blue,
\\Sugar is sweet
\\  And so are you.
\\
;
This syntax doesn’t require a special form for escaping
\\
itself:
const
still_raw =
\\const raw =
\\
\\
Roses are red
\\
\\
Violets are blue,
\\
\\
Sugar is sweet
\\
\\
And so are you.
\\
\\
\\;
\\
;
It nicely dodges indentation problems that plague every other
language with a similar feature. And, the best thing ever:
lexically, each line is a separate token. As Zig has only
line-comments, this means that
\n
is
always
whitespace. Unlike most other languages, Zig can be correctly lexed
in a line-by-line manner.
Raw strings is perhaps the biggest improvement of Zig over Rust.
Rust brute-forces the problem with
r##""##
syntax, which does the required job,
technically, but suffers from the mentioned problems: indentation is
messy, nesting quotes requires adjusting hashes, unclosed raw
literal breaks the following lexical structure completely, and
rustfmt’s formatting of raw strings tends to be rather ugly. On the
plus side, this syntax at least cannot be expressed by a
context-free grammar!
Record Literals
For the record, Zig takes C syntax (not that C would notice):
const
p: Point = .{
.x =
1
,
.y =
2
,
}
The
.{
feels weird! It will make sense by the end of
the post. Here, I want only to note
.x = 1
part, which matches the assignment syntax
obj.x = 1
.
This is great! This means that grepping for
".x = "
gives you
all
instances where a field
is written to. This is hugely valuable: most of usages are reads,
but, to understand the flow of data, you only need to consider
writes. Ability to mechanically partition the entire set of usages
into majority of boring reads and a few interesting writes does
wonders for code comprehension.
Prefix Types
Where Zig departs from C the most is the syntax for types. C uses a
needlessly confusing spiral rule. In Zig, all types are prefix:
u32
// An integer
[
3
]
u32
// An array of three integers
?[
3
]
u32
// An array of three integers or null
// A pointer to...
*
const
?[
3
]
u32
While pointer type is prefix, pointer dereference is postfix, which
is a more natural subject-verb order to read:
ptr.* = 92;
Identifiers
Zig has general syntax for “raw” identifiers:
@"a name which a space"
It is useful to avoid collisions with keywords, or for exporting a
symbol whose name is otherwise not a valid Zig identifier. It is a
bit more to type than Kotlin’s delightful
`a name with a space`
,
but
manages to re-use Zig’s syntax for built-ins (
@TypeOf
)
and strings.
Functions
Like, Rust, Zig goes for
fn foo
function declaration
syntax. This is such a massive improvement over C/Java style
function declarations: it puts
fn
token (which is
completely absent in traditional C family) and function name next to
each other, which means that textual search for
fn name
allows you to quickly find the function. Then Zig adds a little
twist. While in Rust we write
fn
add
(x:
i32
,
i32
)
->
i32
Zig is
fn
add
(x:
i32
,
i32
)
i32
The arrow is gone! Now that I’ve used this for some time, I find
arrow very annoying to type, and adding to the visual noise. Rust
needs the arrow: Rust has lambdas with an inferred return type, and,
in a lambda, the return type is optional. So you need some sort of
an explicit syntax to tell the parser if there is return type:
|| expression;
||
->
Type { }
And its understandable that lambdas and functions would want to use
compatible syntax. But Zig doesn’t have lambdas, so it just makes
the type mandatory. So the main is
pub
fn
main
()
void
{}
Related

data.title: Sunlight-activated material turns PFAS in water into harmless fluoride
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 研究人员在阿德莱德大学开发出一种光激活材料，能够利用阳光降解水中的全氟和多氟烷基物质（PFAS），将其分解为无害的成分，包括氟化物。这种材料为PFAS污染提供了一种低能耗的解决方案，有望用于水处理和环境清理。PFAS因其碳氟键极为牢固，难以分解，长期积累在环境和人体中，带来健康风险。该研究通过优化催化剂，成功打破了PFAS的保护性原子，实现了其完全降解。降解产生的氟化物可用于牙膏或肥料添加剂。研究团队计划进一步改进材料稳定性，以实现大规模应用。这项研究发表在《Small》期刊上。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：材料科学中的循环游戏以及涉及化学物质（如氟化物和镉）的安全性与环境影响

不同观点：
• [nick238] 提出材料科学的两个核心步骤：发明新材料并避免使用铅、镉、汞、砷等有害物质。他通过幽默的方式（使用迷因）指出在处理PFAS（全氟和多氟烷基物质）时，转化产物可能包含镉等有害成分。

• [pxeger1] 对氟化物的安全性提出质疑，指出虽然镉的问题被忽略，但高浓度的氟化物也可能具有急性毒性，甚至可能比致癌的PFAS更糟糕，对环境的影响也可能更严重。

• [ChrisMarshallNY] 以讽刺的口吻质疑氟化物的安全性，并暗示对政府在饮用水处理中不添加氟化物但容忍工业污染物（如PFAS）的双重标准，表现出对政府和工业界的怀疑态度。

• [nraynaud] 对讨论中使用镉化合物处理PFAS的可行性表示困惑，质疑这是否已经是一个被接受或完成的做法，反映出对讨论背景的不确定性。

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了PFAS和氟化物等化学物质对环境和健康的潜在危害，尤其是它们在转化或处理过程中可能产生的次生问题。
• 讨论中涉及对科学研究和政府政策的信任问题，尤其是对某些化学物质的管理和公共健康影响的担忧。
• 争议的焦点主要集中在氟化物的安全性以及在材料科学中使用镉等有害物质的合理性。这些化学物质在处理污染物时可能带来的风险引发了不同评论者的关注和质疑。

August 8, 2025
The GIST
Sunlight-activated material turns PFAS in water into harmless fluoride
by
University of Adelaide
edited by
Sadie Harley
, 																								reviewed by
Robert Egan
Editors' notes
This article has been reviewed according to Science X's
editorial process
and
policies
.
Editors
have highlighted
the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:
fact-checked
peer-reviewed publication
trusted source
proofread
Credit:
Small
(2025). DOI: 10.1002/smll.202504601
Researchers at the University of Adelaide have developed a sunlight-activated material that can degrade per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in water, breaking down the pollutant into harmless components, including fluoride. The work is
published
in the journal
Small
.
The breakthrough discovery represents a promising low-energy solution for PFAS remediation, with potential applications in
water treatment
and environmental cleanup.
"PFAS contamination continues to pose a global health risk, and this research represents a critical step toward safer communities and cleaner ecosystems," says lead researcher Dr. Cameron Shearer, from the University of Adelaide.
"Many water contaminants are degraded by adding a reactive chemical that binds to the carbon. However, in PFAS molecules, the carbon atoms are protected in such a way that makes this process nearly impossible.
"Our team has altered conditions and optimized the catalyst to target the PFAS-protective F atoms, which resulted in complete breakdown of the forever chemicals.
"The produced fluoride can be isolated and used in health care products such as toothpaste or as additives to fertilizers."
PFAS are a group of synthetic chemicals used in non-stick cookware, firefighting foams, and water-repellent fabrics that are extremely resistant to breakdown due to their strong carbon-fluorine bonds and therefore accumulate in the environment and human bodies.
The substances have been linked to serious health issues, including
developmental disorders
, infertility, and cancer.
Recent data shows more than 85% of Australians have detectable PFAS in their blood, and new drinking water guidelines have lowered the safe limits for some PFAS chemicals to just nanograms per liter.
"The materials we have developed through our research could be used as part of PFAS-treatment chains that first capture and concentrate PFAS in water, which can then be degraded through exposure to our light-activated materials," says Dr. Shearer.
"We plan to build on this study through our ongoing work improving the stability of the materials before they can be applied to large-scale systems, a project that is being led by my University of Adelaide colleague, Mahmoud Gharib."
More information:
Mahmoud Adel Hamza et al, CdIn2S4 Micro‐Pyramids for Reductive Photocatalytic Degradation of Perfluorooctanesulfonic Acid,
Small
(2025).
DOI: 10.1002/smll.202504601

data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了大语言模型（LLMs）并非世界模型，尽管它们在很多任务中表现出色。作者通过两个例子说明LLMs缺乏对世界的真正理解。首先，在国际象棋中，LLMs无法有效跟踪棋盘状态，尽管它们阅读了大量棋谱。其次，在图像编辑软件Krita中，LLMs错误解释了图层混合模式，显示其不理解计算机如何处理颜色和透明度。作者强调，LLMs擅长预测文本中的词语顺序，但不具备对现实世界的深入理解。尽管它们可以通过训练数据“偶然”学到一些知识，但这与真正理解世界不同。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLMs（大型语言模型）的“世界模型”能力及其局限性

不同观点：
• **libraryofbabel**：认为LLMs在数学等领域表现出色，具有良好的世界模型。即使模型有时会出错，这并不代表其能力有本质上的限制。出错的原因可能与模型的泛化能力和内部表示的压缩有关。此外，强调通过大量提问和挑选错误来推断模型的局限性并不一定有效。
• **ej88**：认为文章浅显，缺乏对“世界模型”的明确定义。指出不同LLM模型的表现差异显著，未提供具体使用的模型和对话实例使得文章的例子缺乏价值。同时，认为现代LLM对世界有较好的理解，且可以通过实验验证。
• **lordnacho**：通过自身学习经验类比LLMs，认为LLMs可能在提供正确答案时并没有真正理解问题，类似于学生在不完全理解的情况下给出正确答案。LLMs对专家有帮助，但对于非专家可能会产生误导。
• **og_kalu**：引用论文证明LLMs可以很好地模拟国际象棋。
• **imenani**：指出未说明具体使用的LLM模型是个遗憾，因为新发布的LLMs在能力上可能存在显著差异。
• **t0md4n**：提供了一篇论文链接，可能与讨论相关。
• **deadbabe**：幽默地建议不要用LLMs下棋，而是用它们在其他方面提供娱乐或对话。

补充讨论：
• **rishi_devan**：对deadbabe的幽默表示赞赏。
• **GaggiX**：引用视频证明SOTA LLMs可以下出合法的国际象棋走法，质疑文章中对LLMs在国际象棋方面的批评。

争议焦点：
• LLMs是否真正具备“世界模型”能力，尤其是其在不同领域（如数学、国际象棋）的表现是否代表真正的理解，还是仅仅为表面上的正确答案。
• 文章中对LLMs能力的批评是否有效，尤其是在未明确使用哪种模型的情况下。
• LLMs在实际应用中对不同用户（专家 vs 非专家）的帮助和误导可能性。

LLMs arenât world models
August 10th, 2025
I believe that language models arenât world models. Itâs a weak claim â Iâm not saying theyâre useless, or that weâre done
milking them. Itâs also a fuzzy-sounding claim â with its trillion weights, who can prove that thereâs something an LLM isn't a
model of? But I hope to make my claim clear and persuasive enough with some examples.
A friend who plays better chess than me â and knows more math & CS than me - said that he played some moves against a
newly released LLM, and it must be at least as good as him. I said, no way, Iâm going to cRRRush it, in my best Russian accent.
I make a few moves â but unlike him, I don't make good moves
1
, which would be opening book moves it has seen a million times; I make weak moves, which it
hasn't
2
. The thing makes decent moves in
response, with cheerful commentary about how we're attacking this and developing that â until about move 10, when it tries to
move a knight which isn't there, and loses in a few more moves. This was a year or two ago; Iâve just tried this again, and it
lost track of the board state by move 9.
When Iâm saying that LLMs have no world model, I donât mean that they haven't seen enough photos of chess knights, or held a
knight in their greasy fingers; I donât mean the physical world, necessarily. And I obviously donât mean that a machine canât
learn a model of chess, when all leading chess engines use machine learning. I only mean that,
having read a trillion
chess games,
LLMs
, specifically, have not learned that to make legal moves, you need to know where the pieces are on
the board
. Why would they? For predicting the moves or commentary in chess games, which is what theyâre optimized for,
this would help very marginally, if at all.
Of course, nobody uses LLMs as chess engines â so whatever they did learn about chess, they learned entirely âby accidentâ,
without any effort by developers to improve the process for this kind of data. And we could say that the whole argument that
LLMs learn about the world is that they
have
to understand the world
as a side effect of modeling the distribution
of text
â which is soundly refuted by them literally failing to learn the first thing about chess. But maybe we could
charitably assume that LLMs fail this badly with chess for silly reasons you could easily fix, but nobody bothered. So letâs
look at something virtual enough to learn a model of without having greasy fingers to touch it with, but also relevant enough
for developers to try to make it work.
So, for my second example, we will consider the so-called ânormal blending modeâ in image editors like
Krita
â what happens when you put a layer with some partially transparent pixels on top of another
layer? Whatâs the mathematical formula for blending 2 layers? An LLM replied roughly like so:
In Krita Normal blending mode, colors are
not blended using a mathematical formula
. The "Normal" mode
simply
displays the upper layer's color,
potentially affected
by its transparency,
without any interaction or calculation
with the base layer's color.
(It then said how other blending modes
were different and involved mathematical formulas.)
This answer tells us the LLM doesn't know things such as:
Computers work with numbers. A color is represented by a number in a computer.
Therefore, a color cannot be blended by something other than a mathematical formula â nor can it be âaffectedâ without a
âcalculationâ by transparency, another number.
âTransparencyâ is when you can see through something.
âSeeingâ works by sampling the color at various points, and processing that signal.
Therefore, if you can see something through something, like, say, a base layer through an upper layer, then by definition,
the color you will see is affected not only by the color of the upper layer and its degree of transparency, but also by the
color of the base layer â or you wouldnât be
seeing
the base layer, which means that the upper layer is
not at all
transparent, because youâre not seeing through it.
I mean, it sounds stupid to break it down like that, but Iâm not wrong, am I? It really doesnât know any of these things,
does it.
Can you prompt the LLM to explain
alpha blending
properly?
Sure. But that just shows the LLM knows to put the words explaining it after the words asking the question. This capability does
not make the answer above into lesser evidence of the LLM not knowing
the things
as opposed to
the words.
And of course people can be like that, too - eg
much better at the big O
notation and complexity analysis in interviews than on the job
. But I guarantee you that
if you put a gun to their head or
offer them a million dollar bonus for getting it right
, they will do well enough on the job, too. And with 200 billion
thrown at LLM hardware last year, the thing can't complain that it wasn't incentivized to perform
3
.
Of course

data.title: LHC's New Chip Tackles Radiation Challenges
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 《Large Hadron Collider Poised to Receive Major Tech Upgrade》一文报道了LHC即将获得技术升级。由Xu等人设计的新芯片能够在LHC的恶劣环境下工作，并准确转换大量高速粒子碰撞的数据。该芯片将使LHC每秒观察到15亿次碰撞，大大提升其数据处理能力。这一升级将有助于科学家更深入地研究基本粒子物理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于模拟-数字转换器（ADC）阶段在辐射环境中的表现以及文章标题的拼写问题

不同观点：
• magicalhippo认为，根据引用的论文，该模拟-数字转换器设计具有一定的抗辐射能力。设计中采用的9个子范围（3.2位）MDAC和12位两阶段SAR架构，能够通过无记忆的MDAC和SAR来缓解动态范围的要求。由于LAr脉冲形状是已知的，可以通过离线数据分析来纠正由于单事件翻转（SEUs）引起的瞬态错误，这意味着辐射只会影响个别数据样本。

• thrance则关注文章标题中的拼写问题，指出文章标题中将"Hadron"误拼写为"Hardon"，这是一个显而易见的错误。

补充讨论：
- magicalhippo引用的论文提供了技术细节，强调了设计中对辐射引发错误的可容忍性和纠正能力。
- thrance的评论则偏向于对文章标题拼写错误的调侃，没有涉及技术内容，属于对文章表层问题的关注。
- 争议焦点并不在于技术实现，而在于文章标题的拼写错误，这是一种表面的、非技术性的争议。

data.title: Employees spotting problems help the business, but leaders empower flatterers
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了两项研究，发现领导者往往不愿意赋予那些对现状提出质疑的员工更多权力，即使这些员工对发现问题和提出解决方案至关重要。文章区分了两种行为：一种是“挑战声音”，即员工对领导决策提出质疑；另一种是“支持声音”，即员工支持现状并赞美工作环境。研究显示，领导者通常更倾向于赋予那些使用支持声音的员工更多权力，因为他们不认为这些员工对其领导地位构成威胁。然而，如果使用挑战声音的员工同时表现出高度的帮助行为，如在领导工作负担重时伸出援手，他们就不会被视为威胁。文章建议，领导者应意识到赋予挑战现状的员工权力可能对公司有利，而员工则应在提出问题的同时展示对领导的帮助行为。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：控制与权力在组织和个人行为中的作用，以及其对现状和创新的影响。

不同观点：
• WarOnPrivacy认为，控制欲在许多情况下超过了其他重要因素，如利润。他举例说明版权极端主义者为了控制权而放弃利润，以及工会因权力腐败的例子。他还提到招聘门户自动排除某些申请人的现象，并指出许多人抱怨但同时也是潜在的问题解决者，他们的意见常被忽视。

• icegreentea2指出，领导者对挑战现状的人产生负面反应，因为这些人被视为威胁。除非挑战者展现出改善现状的强烈意愿，才会被接受。这种行为被视为人类自然的自我保护反应，领导者倾向于将自我认同与现状绑定。

• nudgeOrnurture认为，许多问题被选择性忽视，以维持财务平衡或保护管理层。他引用了一种类似苏联后期管理的现象，即信息隐瞒和责任推卸。他还提到企业中的等级制度往往只为讨好上级，而无实际功能，并担忧这种趋势会导致腐败。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于控制欲对组织和个人的影响。WarOnPrivacy强调控制欲的强大和普遍性，而icegreentea2和nudgeOrnurture则关注控制欲如何影响领导者的决策和组织结构。

• 讨论中还涉及等级制度和权力结构的有效性与腐败问题。nudgeOrnurture特别提到了企业等级制度的功能失调和信息隐瞒现象，而WarOnPrivacy则关注招聘中的自动排除机制。

• 另一个值得注意的点是关于挑战现状的人的角色。icegreentea2认为这些人需要展现改善意图才能被接受，而WarOnPrivacy则指出，许多抱怨者实际上也是潜在的解决方案提供者，但他们的意见常被忽视。

这些观点共同揭示了控制欲和权力结构在组织行为中的复杂影响，以及对创新和改善的潜在阻碍。

Credit: Unsplash/CC0 Public Domain
Two new studies find that leaders are less likely to empower followers who raise concerns about workplace decisions, even though these "challenging voice" employees play a critical role in highlighting problems and identifying solutions. The studies also outline what drives these decisions.
"We know that
employee
performance improves and employee turnover declines when employees are empowered—that's good," says Bradley Kirkman, co-author of a paper on the two studies. "We also know that having employees who use challenging voice are also beneficial to the bottom line—because this leads employees to be more creative, feel greater responsibility, innovate more, and share knowledge more often."
So why are
leaders
not embracing this approach?
"That's what we wanted to explore with these studies," says Kirkman, who is the General (Ret.) H. Hugh Shelton Distinguished Professor of Leadership in North Carolina State University's Poole College of Management.
At issue are behaviors known as "challenging voice" and "supportive voice." Challenging voice refers to instances when an employee raises concerns about the status quo: potentially pushing back against leadership decisions, identifying potential problems with corporate strategy, etc. Supportive voice refers to instances when an employee is supporting the status quo: encouraging leaders, praising the workplace, and so on.
For the first study, the researchers enlisted 143 professional MBAs across multiple industries in China. The researchers also enlisted 266 employees who worked for those MBAs. In total, the study included 315 dyads consisting of a leader and a follower. The leaders and followers each completed three surveys over the course of six weeks. Each survey was designed to capture the behavior of both leaders and followers, and how the behavior of the followers influenced the behavior of leaders and how they viewed the followers.
For the second study, researchers recruited 528 adults in the United States. These study participants were given a common scenario in which they were a corporate leader and then asked questions aimed at assessing the participant's willingness to empower an employee. However, study participants were given different descriptions of the employee's behavior.
The researchers manipulated variables to give each participant one of six different employee descriptions. Participants were randomly assigned to a situation where the employee exhibited either challenging voice or supportive voice. Participants were then randomly assigned to scenarios in which the employee exhibited high or low challenging voice or high or low supportive voice (i.e., exhibited a range of challenging or supportive behaviors), along with high or low levels of behavior that helped the leader.
"The results were consistent across both studies," Kirkman says. "Employees who exhibited challenging voice were less likely to be empowered; employees who use supportive voice were more likely to be empowered. In other words, managers favored bootlickers over boat-rockers.
"The reasons for this behavior were also the same in both studies," Kirkman says. "Managers perceived employees who used challenging voice as threats to their leadership. On the other hand, leaders perceived the use of supportive voice as an indication that the employee shared the manager's goals."

主要讨论点：Namedrop newsletter的服务模式及公平性

不同观点：
• 支持观点1：Namedrop提供的服务对创业者有帮助。评论者提到，该 newsletter 提供有创意的名字和未注册的域名，对 startup 创始人们非常有用。论据包括，越来越多的创业者愿意使用各种类型的域名扩展，而 Namedrop 正好满足这一需求。
   
• 支持观点2：随机发送邮件的公平性。评论者解释说，为了保证公平，邮件会在随机时间发送，这样每个人都有公平的机会获得好的域名。这是因为好的域名通常很快就会被抢注。

• 潜在观点：鼓励反馈。评论者表示，如果有人根据 newsletter 中的名字创建了有趣的项目，他们很愿意听到相关消息。这表明对用户反馈和成功案例持开放态度，并希望通过这种方式促进互动和交流。

• 时间公平性策略：通过随机时间发送邮件来保证公平竞争，这一策略旨在防止某些人总是在第一时间抢到最好的域名。

没有明显的争议焦点，整体讨论集中于服务的好处和公平性策略的合理性。

data.title: Procrastination and the Bikeshed Effect (2009)
data.author: hypeatei
data.article_summary: 《Producing Open Source Software》是一本关于如何成功运行自由软件项目的优秀参考书，涵盖了项目管理的各个方面，尤其强调了沟通的重要性。书中指出，开源项目中如果管理不善，可能会吸引一些更热衷于讨论而非编写代码的开发者，这就是所谓的"自行车棚效应"（Bikeshed Effect）。这种效应指的是，对于简单易懂的技术问题或软性话题（如组织、宣传、资金等），讨论往往冗长且难以达成共识，因为每个人都可以参与讨论，且没有明确的判断标准。这种讨论实际上是一种拖延形式，甚至会吸引高技术开发者，影响项目进展。书中建议，应尽快从抽象讨论转向实际构建，以提高项目效率。

44855252.article_content:
The book
Producing Open Source Software
: How to Run a Successful Free Software Project is a
fantastic reference for anyone involved in a software project
– whether you’re running the show or not.
In addition to the dead-tree edition, the book is available in an appropriately open source free format at
the official website
. The entire book is great, and worth a thorough read, even if you think open source
is communism
.
My favorite chapter is
the one on communication
. While important on any software project, communication is especially vital on open source projects, which are “bewilderingly diverse both in audiences and communication mechanisms.” One particular pitfall of open source projects is that, if you don’t manage the project carefully, you can tend to attract developers who
are more interested in discussion
than writing code. It’s a subtle but pernicious problem – communication gone wrong.
Although discussion can meander in any topic, the probability of meandering goes up as the technical difficulty of the topic goes down. After all, the greater the technical difficulty, the fewer participants can really follow what’s going on. Those who can are likely to be the most experienced developers, who have already taken part in such discussions thousands of times before, and know what sort of behavior is likely to lead to a consensus everyone can live with.
Thus, consensus is hardest to achieve in technical questions that are simple to understand and easy to have an opinion about, and in “soft” topics such as organization, publicity, funding, etc. People can participate in those arguments forever, because there are no qualifications necessary for doing so, no clear ways to decide (even afterward) if a decision was right or wrong, and because simply outwaiting other discussants is sometimes a successful tactic.
The principle that the amount of discussion is inversely proportional to the complexity of the topic has been around for a long time, and is known informally as
the Bikeshed Effect
.
We’ve struggled with this on
Stack Overflow
, too. The broad soft questions tend to get much more interest and attention than the narrow, technical coding questions that we originally intended the site for. We’ve made adjustments, but it’s an unavoidable aspect of group dynamics. Who are we kidding? It’s
fun
to discuss what color the bikeshed should be painted. Everyone has an opinion about their favorite color scheme.
What many people don’t realize is that the bikeshed effect is, in fact,
a form of procrastination
. And it can suck in highly technical developers, along with everyone else.
The psychologists handed out questionnaires to a group of students and asked them to respond by e-mail within three weeks. All the questions had to do with rather mundane tasks like opening a bank account and keeping a diary, but different students were given different instructions for answering the questions. Some thought and wrote about what each activity implied about personal traits: what kind of person has a bank account, for example. Others wrote simply about the nuts and bolts of doing each activity: speaking to a bank officer, filling out forms, making an initial deposit, and so forth. The idea was to
get some students thinking abstractly and others concretely
. Then the psychologists waited. And in some cases, waited and waited. They recorded all the response times to see if there was a difference between the two groups, and indeed there was a significant difference.
The findings, reported in Psychological Science, a journal of the Association for Psychological Science, were very clear. Even though all of the students were being paid upon completion,
those who thought about the questions abstractly were much more likely to procrastinate – and in fact some never got around to the assignment at all.
By contrast, those who were focused on the how, when and where of doing the task e-mailed their responses much sooner, suggesting that they hopped right on the assignment rather than delaying it.
This is one reason why I’m so down on
architecture astronauts
. I find that
the amount of discussion on a software feature is inversely proportional to its value
. Sure, have some initial discussion to figure out your direction, but the sooner you can get away from airy abstractions, and down to the nuts and bolts of
building the damn thing
, the better off you – and your project – will be.
Put another way, what’s
the hardest thing you have to do every day?
Deciding what to ignore, so you can stop procrastinating and
get stuff done
. The next time you feel yourself getting drawn into a protracted bikeshed discussion, consider: shouldn’t you be
building something instead?

data.title: Show HN: Kitten TTS – 25MB CPU-Only, Open-Source TTS Model
data.author: divamgupta
data.article_summary: KittenTTS 是一个开源的轻量级文本到语音（TTS）模型，模型大小不到25MB，专为高品质语音合成和轻量部署设计。它具有超轻量、CPU优化、高品质声音和快速推理等特点，无需GPU即可在任何设备上运行。目前处于开发者预览阶段，提供多个优质声音选项。安装可通过 `pip` 完成，基本用法包括生成语音和保存音频文件。系统要求宽泛，几乎适用于所有设备。未来计划包括发布完全训练的模型权重、移动SDK和网页版本。该项目基于Apache-2.0许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：KittenTTS模型的性能、质量、应用场景及技术挑战

不同观点：
• 支持者认为KittenTTS代表了未来的方向，特别是能够在廉价、普遍的硬件上运行小型离线ML模型。这种模型易于集成到设备和应用程序中，并且不受限于硬件和云服务（如nine_k、MutedEstate45）。
• 有人关注模型的性能表现，提供了具体的基准测试数据，显示模型在不同文本长度下的音频生成速度和初始延迟，整体表现较为稳定（如peanut_merchant）。
• 批评者指出，虽然模型本身只有25MB，但依赖的库和环境安装后占用的空间远超25MB，且在不同机器上的Python版本兼容性问题导致安装困难（如antsol、klipklop）。
• 对于音质，部分用户认为KittenTTS的音质不如其他TTS模型（如fish-speech和f5-tts），尤其是与需要GPU支持的高质量模型相比，音质差距明显（如sandreas、wkat4242）。
• 部分用户对模型的延迟问题表示关注，尤其是希望在自然对话中实现流畅的语音交互（如keyle）。
• 也有用户对模型的跨语言支持表示关注，询问是否能训练模型支持其他语言（如spapas82）。

补充讨论：
• 有用户指出KittenTTS的开源许可（Apache-2.0）使其在嵌入式设备和低功耗设备中具有广泛应用潜力，解决了硬件和许可问题（如MutedEstate45）。
• 一些用户分享了在实际项目中使用其他TTS模型的经验，如KokoroTTS和Whisper（用于语音转文本），并表达了对更好TTS模型的期待（如vahid4m、wkat4242）。
• 技术问题也被提及，如TTS模型在处理某些文本格式时的错误（如dr_kiszonka对"i.e."被读作"for example"的疑问）。
• 一些用户对项目的未来发展表示期待，尤其是希望看到更多能在CPU上高效运行的优秀模型（如toisanji）。

44807868.article_summary: KittenTTS 是一个开源的轻量级文本到语音（TTS）模型，模型大小不到25MB，专为高品质语音合成和轻量部署设计。它具有超轻量、CPU优化、高品质声音和快速推理等特点，无需GPU即可在任何设备上运行。目前处于开发者预览阶段，提供多个优质声音选项。安装可通过 `pip` 完成，基本用法包括生成语音和保存音频文件。系统要求宽泛，几乎适用于所有设备。未来计划包括发布完全训练的模型权重、移动SDK和网页版本。该项目基于Apache-2.0许可证。
44807868.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：KittenTTS模型的性能、质量、应用场景及技术挑战

不同观点：
• 支持者认为KittenTTS代表了未来的方向，特别是能够在廉价、普遍的硬件上运行小型离线ML模型。这种模型易于集成到设备和应用程序中，并且不受限于硬件和云服务（如nine_k、MutedEstate45）。
• 有人关注模型的性能表现，提供了具体的基准测试数据，显示模型在不同文本长度下的音频生成速度和初始延迟，整体表现较为稳定（如peanut_merchant）。
• 批评者指出，虽然模型本身只有25MB，但依赖的库和环境安装后占用的空间远超25MB，且在不同机器上的Python版本兼容性问题导致安装困难（如antsol、klipklop）。
• 对于音质，部分用户认为KittenTTS的音质不如其他TTS模型（如fish-speech和f5-tts），尤其是与需要GPU支持的高质量模型相比，音质差距明显（如sandreas、wkat4242）。
• 部分用户对模型的延迟问题表示关注，尤其是希望在自然对话中实现流畅的语音交互（如keyle）。
• 也有用户对模型的跨语言支持表示关注，询问是否能训练模型支持其他语言（如spapas82）。

补充讨论：
• 有用户指出KittenTTS的开源许可（Apache-2.0）使其在嵌入式设备和低功耗设备中具有广泛应用潜力，解决了硬件和许可问题（如MutedEstate45）。
• 一些用户分享了在实际项目中使用其他TTS模型的经验，如KokoroTTS和Whisper（用于语音转文本），并表达了对更好TTS模型的期待（如vahid4m、wkat4242）。
• 技术问题也被提及，如TTS模型在处理某些文本格式时的错误（如dr_kiszonka对"i.e."被读作"for example"的疑问）。
• 一些用户对项目的未来发展表示期待，尤其是希望看到更多能在CPU上高效运行的优秀模型（如toisanji）。

data.author: inglor_cz

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI辅助编程的最佳实践和工具选择  

不同观点：  
• **手动输入代码以加深理解**  
  - mikewarot认为应亲自输入代码而非复制粘贴，以避免快速产生遗留代码。  
  - MilnerRoute提到DHH（Ruby on Rails创始人）也支持手动输入AI建议，认为这能加深记忆和理解。  

• **AI工具的选择与比较**  
  - cellis指出Claude Code在工程上不如Cursor易用，但更便宜；Cursor的模型组合（尤其是Sonnet）表现优于GPT-5。  
  - viraptor推荐Cursor为当前默认选择，价格合理且功能完善；Aider结合特定提供商也是不错选择。  
  - PretzelPirate推荐Github Copilot的免费层作为入门尝试。  

• **使用AI的注意事项**  
  - the__alchemist提出具体建议：避免让AI创建函数签名或结构体，明确指令不改变变量名，严格控制上下文范围。  
  - uberman提到免费层适合小任务，但需验证和理解结果。  

补充讨论：  
• **争议焦点**：AI辅助编程是加速开发还是阻碍学习？  
  - MilnerRoute提到DHH的观点：AI可以辅助学习，也可能剥夺学习机会，取决于使用方式（快速完成 vs 深度理解）。  
  - snaga提到基于规范的开发（如Gemini-CLI）有助于理解AI辅助编程的运作方式。  

• **工具功能差异**：  
  - cellis批评GPT-5倾向于“说而不做”，而Gemini 2.5 Pro在复杂代码库的调试中表现最佳。  
  - viraptor提醒注意付费模式，避免自动续费陷阱。

data.author: gaws
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：互联网网站设计的变化、工具的实用性与局限、以及互联网商业化趋势

不同观点：
• [kachapopopow] 认为整个互联网已经变成了一个销售商品的入口，表达了对互联网过度商业化的担忧。
• [dathery] 对工具的视觉化效果表示赞赏，并提议使用实际的网页截图（如论坛、图片托管网站等）来增强工具的怀旧和实用性，分享了个人收藏多年截图的经历。
• [karpour] 指出当今的网页设计缺乏创意，99%的网站使用相同的标准布局，怀念过去网页设计作为艺术形式的时代，希望看到更多打破常规的设计。
• [Fade_Dance] 认为当前的工具展示了主流网站，但缺乏小众或独特网站的发现，建议引入AI来筛选小众或历史悠久的网站。

补充讨论：
• [hn-user-42] 和 [netsharc] 提供了与主题相关但不深入的观点，前者分享了一个有趣的缩放图片链接，后者提到了与百万美元首页的关联，增加了讨论的历史背景。
• [blendaddict] 对工具表示赞赏，但也提到现代网站设计趋同的问题，呼应了 [karpour] 的观点。
• [awb] 建议从颜色、布局、功能、字体、照片等方面分析数据集，以统计测量网页设计的独特性或创造力。
• [starchild3001] 反驳了“死互联网理论”，并提到大多数流行网页在6个月内会发生变化，且这种变化无法由机器人完成，暗示了人类创造力的持续存在。
• [milancurcic] 和 [LorenDB] 指出了工具的技术问题，前者提到工具破坏了浏览器的后退按钮，后者提到被Cloudflare Family DNS阻止访问。
• [Brajeshwar] 感谢工具中包含了自己的网站，这是一个对个人参与的积极反馈。
• [Unearned5161] 和 [latchkey] 提供了对工具体验的具体反馈，前者喜欢灰色的网站，因其提示即将出现的弹出窗口，后者提到要求添加网站后收到了垃圾邮件。
• [socalgal2] 指出工具展示的并非真正的截图，认为真正的截图应显示窗口、菜单等，提出了工具改进的方向。

争议焦点：
• 现代网站设计的趋同与创意缺失：[karpour]、[blendaddict] 和 [Fade_Dance] 对现代网页设计缺乏独特性和创意表示不满，而 [starchild3001] 则认为互联网的活力和变化仍然存在。
• 工具的实用性与技术问题：[milancurcic] 和 [LorenDB] 指出了工具的技术问题，如破坏浏览器后退按钮和被DNS阻止，而 [dathery] 和 [awb] 则提出了改进工具的建议，如使用实际截图和分析数据集。

总结：讨论围绕互联网的商业化趋势、网站设计的趋同与创意缺失、工具的实用性与技术问题展开，参与者提供了多样化的观点和具体反馈。

data.title: 1910: The year the modern world lost its mind
data.author: purgator
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了1910年前后技术迅猛发展带来的社会焦虑与人性变化。作者德里克·汤普森通过历史书籍《眩晕的年代：1900-1914年的欧洲》分析了20世纪初汽车、飞机、自行车等新技术的出现如何改变了人们的生活方式和思维方式，引发了广泛的焦虑情绪。当时的人们感到世界变化太快，无法适应。这种快速发展不仅导致精神崩溃，还影响了艺术创作。作者指出，虽然历史不会重演，但过去与现在的挑战有许多相似之处，研究历史可以帮助我们理解当下。文章强调了技术进步带来的社会心理影响以及人类对快速变化的适应问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：技术和社会变革对人类的影响，特别是在工业革命及其后续时期的快速变化。

不同观点：
• nickdothutton提到，在工业革命早期，人们抱怨远处引擎的振动影响睡眠，尽管这些问题在他们阅读相关报道之前并未意识到，暗示心理因素可能影响了生理感受。
• alexpotato强调了技术对社会影响的连续性，特别是通过《The Victorian Internet》一书展示了电报如何迅速改变了商业、金融市场和法律事务。
• derbOac指出公共健康领域的显著进步，尤其是在减少婴儿死亡率和传染病控制方面，认为过去150-200年的变化是历史上前所未有的。
• eschulz通过古代对日晷的抱怨类比现代对新技术的反应，引用Plautus的文字显示人们对时间分割的抵触。
• cgh和ofalkaed推荐Pynchon的《Against the Day》作为探索技术变革对社会影响的文学作品，特别是对摄影和电影发展的处理，展示了技术对社会和个人生活的深远影响。
• leeoniya引用Pascal的观点，认为人类无法安静独处是许多问题的根源，并通过"速度是种病"的引述讨论现代社会对速度和变化的焦虑。
• ChrisMarshallNY提到Wright兄弟作为自行车机械师的背景，暗示自行车技术对早期航空的影响。
• theragra对比美国和俄罗斯帝国的变化速度，强调俄罗斯经历了多次革命和战争，以及艺术和文化的快速发展。
• GOD_Over_Djinn分享了Stravinsky的《The Rite of Spring》首演时观众的激烈反应，展示了新艺术形式引发的社会冲突。
• stevenfoster提到Theodore Roosevelt利用电报系统与全国保持联系，展示了技术在政治领导中的应用。
• russellbeattie设想未来世代对内燃机的恐怖反应，通过夸张的描述突显现代技术对环境的负面影响。
• abbadadda质疑现代技术是否摧毁了人性，提出了对技术快速发展的批判性思考。
• marc_abonce指出文章未包括墨西哥革命，认为这也是一个值得讨论的1910年开始的重要历史事件。
• komali2通过历史上的道德批判对比现代对性别角色的讨论，暗示对新技术的道德恐慌可能是不同时代的共同特征。

补充讨论：
- 技术变革对社会各方面的深远影响，包括商业、法律、艺术和健康。
- 历史上对新技术和新社会现象的道德恐慌和批判。
- 不同国家和地区在面对技术和社会变革时的不同经历和速度。
- 文学作品和艺术形式在反映和探索技术变革中的作用。

1910: The Year the Modern World Lost Its Mind
What one of my favorite history books about my favorite historical period—turn-of-the-century American—tells us about technology, anxiety, and human nature
Derek Thompson
Aug 10, 2025
171
Share this post
Derek Thompson

More
5
19
Share
“Automobilism is an illness, a mental illness. This illness has a pretty name: speed... [Man] can no longer stand still, he shivers, his nerves tense like springs, impatient to get going once he has arrived somewhere because it is not somewhere else, somewhere else, always somewhere else.”
- Octave Mirbeau, French novelist, 1910
About today’s piece: When we hear about technological change and social crisis in the 21st century, it is easy to imagine that we are living through a special period of history. But many eras have grappled with the problems that seem to uniquely plague our own. The beginning of the 20th century was a period of speed and technological splendor (the automobile! the airplane! the bicycle!), shattered nerves, mass anxiety, and a widespread sense that the world had been forever knocked off its historical axis: a familiar stew of ideas. I think we can learn a lot about the present by studying historical periods whose challenges rhyme with our own.
Welcome back to The Sunday Morning Post!
My favorite period of history is the 30- to 40-year span between the end of the 19th century and the early innings of the 20th century. It was an era of incredible change. From
Abundance
:
Imagine going to sleep in 1875 in New York City and waking up thirty years later. As you shut your eyes, there is no electric lighting, Coca-Cola, basketball, or aspirin. There are no cars or “sneakers.” The tallest building in Manhattan is a church.
When you wake up in 1905, the city has been remade with towering steel-skeleton buildings called “skyscrapers.” The streets are filled with novelty: automobiles powered by new internal combustion engines, people riding bicycles in rubber-soled shoes—all recent innovations. The Sears catalog, the cardboard box, and aspirin are  new arrivals. People have enjoyed their first sip of Coca-Cola and their first bite of what we now call an American hamburger. The Wright brothers have flown the first airplane. When you passed into slumber, nobody had taken a picture with a Kodak camera or used a machine that made motion pictures, or bought a device to play recorded music. By 1905, we have the first commercial versions of all three—the simple box camera, the cinematograph,  and the phonograph.
No book on turn-of-the-century history has influenced me more, or brought me more joy, than
The Vertigo Years: Europe 1900-1914
by Philipp Blom. I think it might be the most underrated history book ever written.
1
In my favorite chapters focusing on the years around 1910
2
, Blom describes how turn-of-the-century technology changed the way people thought about art and human nature and how it contributed to a nervous breakdown across the west. Disoriented by the speed of modern times, Europeans and Americans suffered from record-high rates of anxiety and a sense that our inventions had destroyed our humanity. Meanwhile, some artists channeled this disorientation to create some of the greatest art of all time.
In today’s TSMP, I want to share with you my favorite passages and lessons from
The Vertigo Years
, most of which come from the chapter on the year 1910. Great history books remind us that while history never repeats itself, its themes never stop rhyming, and we would all do well to listen with open ears. I’ve tried to limit my summary to areas of overlap between the early 1900s and the 2020s, but I’m not going to press the similarities too hard throughout the piece. You’re going to have to recognize them for yourself.
This Substack is reader-supported. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
Subscribe
1. People in 1910 felt the world was moving much too fast
Transportation technology remade the west in a few short decades between the 1880s and 1910. A “bicycle craze” swept America in the 1890s. The Wright Brothers took flight in 1903. The first Model Ts rolled off Ford’s production lines in 1908. In Europe, cars quickly transformed the physical environment. The number of automobiles in France increased from about 3,000 in 1900 to 100,000 by 1914. That year, Ford's factory in Detroit produced and sold more than 300,000 Model Ts.
Model T, Wikimedia Commons

data.title: Fight Chat Control
data.author: tokai
data.article_summary: 欧盟的"Chat Control"提案要求扫描所有私人数字通信，包括加密消息和照片，威胁到欧盟公民的隐私权和数字安全。该提案获得部分成员国支持，但遭到反对和未决定国家的抵制。自动扫描不需怀疑或例外，甚至涉及加密通信，可能破坏加密技术，使数据暴露给黑客和不法分子。自动化扫描还可能误判无辜内容，导致错误指控。此外，大规模监控无助于保护儿童，反而削弱安全，分散资源。该政策可能树立全球先例，鼓励其他国家推行侵入性监控，破坏隐私和言论自由。民众需联系欧洲议会议员，反对大规模监控。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧盟强制年龄验证法律及其潜在影响，特别是涉及监狱刑罚的条款，以及对民主和隐私的威胁。

不同观点：
• [throwaway89201] 指出欧洲议会已经通过了一项法律修正案，要求对色情内容实施强制年龄验证，违反者将面临最高一年的监禁。该用户担心该法案可能不会通过第二次阅读。
• [lucideer] 提供了更多背景信息，指出欧盟理事会在该法规的推动中拥有更多权力，并认为该网站误导了大多数欧洲议会议员的立场。该用户怀疑许多议员已经知道并强烈反对这项法案，但质疑议会是否有足够权力阻止它。
• [Disposal8433] 表示在法国，很多人都支持这项法案，包括所谓的左派，个人无力改变现状，只能通过捐款支持某些隐私项目。
• [Centigonal] 将欧盟的监控措施与美国的监控项目进行比较，质疑是否有任何政权不试图以某种理由对公民进行大规模监控。
• [101008] 对欧盟政治家豁免于这种监控表示愤怒，认为普通公民的隐私权被剥夺，而政治家却享有隐私保护。
• [ncr100] 强烈反对这项政策，称之为思想警察，并质疑权力持有者在经济增长末期是否都在加强监控和执法。
• [rossant] 引用了一个链接，指出许多以“保护儿童”为名的政策实际上是错误的。
• [kratom_sandwich] 询问有哪些组织在对抗聊天控制，可以进行捐款支持。
• [isoprophlex] 对类似的法案多次尝试通过表示愤怒和无奈。
• [mustaphah] 讽刺地指出，欧盟在捍卫人权方面做得很好，除非涉及到私人信息。
• [dachris] 讽刺英国脱欧后在隐私监控方面走得更远，带有幽默意味。
• [thesdev] 指出个别欧洲议会议员的立场与国家政府的立场并不完全一致，纠正对网站内容的误解。
• [nomilk] 指出法律通常承认隐私的神圣性，但立法者却希望能够查看所有人的私人信息，这是一种奇怪的矛盾。
• [alphazard] 询问个人在没有进一步协调的情况下，可以采取哪些实际措施来避免这项政策的影响，比如使用特定的Android发行版或自定义构建。
• [setnone] 提供了一个资源链接，包括欧洲议会关于“数字技术作为镇压和社会控制手段”的研究。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于强制年龄验证法案的合理性及其潜在的隐私侵犯问题。
• 用户普遍对法案的监控和刑罚条款表示强烈反对，认为这是对个人隐私的严重威胁。
• 一些用户提供了背景信息和资源链接，帮助其他人更好地理解和对抗这项政策。
• 讨论中多次提到对民主失效和隐私权被剥夺的无奈和愤怒。

data.title: Show HN: Bolt – A super-fast, statically-typed scripting language written in C
data.author: beariish
data.article_summary: Bolt是一款高性能、实时优化、静态类型的嵌入式编程语言，采用C语言实现，具有快速编译、轻量化和易嵌入等特点。它支持丰富的类型系统，能够提前捕获错误，并可轻松与原生代码集成。Bolt依赖于C标准库和libm，提供文件和系统IO等模块，但这些可以灵活配置。目前，Bolt主要支持x64架构，并提供CMake构建系统生成静态库和CLI工具。尽管Bolt尚未稳定，可能存在编译器错误，但它在MSVC、GCC和Clang上基本功能正常。Bolt使用MIT许可证，并鼓励贡献者提交错误修复和优化，但新功能需经过充分讨论和论证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Bolt语言设计和实现的多个方面展开的讨论，包括性能优化、语法设计、嵌入式系统支持、错误处理以及与其他语言的比较。

不同观点：
• **性能优化和解释器设计**：
  ◦ [haberman] 支持在Bolt的解释器中使用尾调用优化，并引用了相关博客文章，展示了这种技术如何在其他语言中提升性能。
  ◦ [JonChesterfield] 则对尾调用优化持怀疑态度，认为直接在字节码中处理函数标识符可能更有效，并建议参考WASM解释器和Luajit的实现。

• **语法设计和导入声明**：
  ◦ [perlgeek] 反对将导入符号放在导入语句的首位，认为这样会掩盖符号的来源，建议参考Java、Python和Perl等语言的做法。
  ◦ Typescript是一个例外，它采用类似Bolt的导入语法。

• **嵌入式系统支持**：
  ◦ [conaclos] 指出Bolt依赖双精度浮点数，不适合嵌入式系统，这类系统通常不支持浮点运算。
  ◦ [MobiusHorizons] 补充说明，在开发社区中，“嵌入式场景”通常被理解为嵌入式系统，而非嵌入式解释器。

• **内存管理和错误处理**：
  ◦ [cookiengineer] 对Bolt的返回签名、内存管理、引用/指针支持提出疑问，并建议参考Koka语言的效应基于错误类型系统。
  ◦ 对Bolt的错误处理方式表示担忧，认为在调试大型代码库时可能会遇到困难。

• **与其他语言的比较和命名**：
  ◦ [themonsu] 对Bolt的命名表示不满，建议换个名字。
  ◦ [freeopinion] 建议将Bolt与Q语言进行对比测试，以增加彼此的曝光度。

• **语法建议和功能需求**：
  ◦ [tayistay] 建议增加`var`关键字，以区分可变和不可变变量声明。
  ◦ [Fraterkes] 对Bolt的内存占用和创建快速脚本语言的过程感兴趣，并询问相关文档。
  ◦ [merksoftworks] 关注Bolt在MacOS和aarm64架构上的可移植性问题。
  ◦ [memophysic] 询问Bolt对断点和调试服务器的支持情况。

• **其他评论**：
  ◦ [kiririn] 认为Bolt让人联想到Pawn语言。
  ◦ [Forgret] 对Bolt的发展表示祝福，并希望它能变得流行。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Bolt的性能声称和实际优化手段，尤其是尾调用优化的适用性和效果。
• 对语法设计的不同偏好反映了不同开发者的使用习惯和编程语言背景。
• 嵌入式系统的支持问题引发了对Bolt应用场景的进一步思考。
• 对内存管理和错误处理的讨论揭示了Bolt在实际应用中可能遇到的挑战。

(
"The answer is"
,
result
)
}
}
Features
Lightning-fast performance
, outperforming other languages in its class
Compact implementation, leaving a minimal impact on build size while remaining consise enough to browse.
Blazingly quick compilation, plow through code at over 500kloc/thread/second. That's 50'000 lines in the blink of an eye.
Ease of embedding, only a handful of lines to get going
Rich type system to catch errors before code is ran, with plenty of support for extending it from native code
Embed-first design, prioritizing inter-language performance and agility
Links

Notable Bolt users
Dependencies
Bolt only depends on the C standard library as well as
libm
on Unix-based systems.
Some standard library modules include things like file and system IO, but these can be disabled easily.
By default, Bolt sets up an environment that uses
malloc
/
realloc
/
free
, but this is also easy to configure.
Bolt also embeds my other library
picomatch
for regex parsing
Minimal embedding example
The
bolt-cli
program provides a very consice example of how to embed bolt an an application, see the
Bolt embedding guide
for more details.
Language examples
The
examples
folder contains a few short examples of ideomatically written bolt code. Check out the
tests
and
benchmarks
folders as wel for some more in-depth language overview.
Building
Bolt currently only builds on x64. 32-bit architectures are explicitly not supported, arm and riscv are untested.
Running
cmake
in the root directory of the project will generate a static library for the language, as well as the CLI tool.
For more information and options regarding embedding Bolt in your application, see
bt_config.h

Bolt is a very opinionated project, and any contributions should take the vision into account.
Bugfixes are likely to be accepted as long as they're within reason and don't change any expected behaviour. Adding tests in case of regression is very much appreciated as well. A clean run of
/tests/all

Optimizations may also be accepted for minor versions under similar criteria. A before/after run of

data.title: Events
data.author: aanthonymax
data.article_summary:
这篇文章简要介绍了JavaScript中的事件处理。事件是系统中发生的动作，浏览器会通知这些事件，使开发者能够通过编写代码做出响应。文章讲解了事件的基本概念，包括什么是事件、如何使用`addEventListener()`设置事件处理器、以及为何不推荐使用内联事件处理属性。

事件可以通过`addEventListener()`方法来监听，当事件触发时，指定的事件处理函数会被调用。例如，点击按钮后，背景颜色可以随机变化。文章还提到可以监听多种不同的事件，如`mouseover`、`keydown`等。通过示例代码，文章展示了如何为按钮的点击事件添加事件监听器，并演示了事件处理过程。

总结：事件是浏览器中的信号，开发者可以使用`addEventListener()`来监听和响应这些事件。

Overview: Dynamic scripting with JavaScript

Events are things that happen in the system you are programming, which the system tells you about so your code can react to them.
For example, if the user clicks a button on a webpage, you might want to react to that action by displaying an information box.
In this article, we discuss some important concepts surrounding events, and look at the fundamentals of how they work in browsers.
Prerequisites:
An understanding of
HTML
and the
fundamentals of CSS
, familiarity with JavaScript basics as covered in previous lessons.
Learning outcomes:
What events are â a signal fired by the browser when something significant happens, which the developer can run some code in response to.
Setting up event handlers using
addEventListener()
(and
removeEventListener()
) and event handler properties.
Inline event handler attributes, and why you shouldn't use them.
Event objects.
What is an event?
Events are things that happen in the system you are programming â the system produces (or "fires") a signal of some kind when an event occurs, and provides a mechanism by which an action can be automatically taken (that is, some code running) when the event occurs.
Events are fired inside the browser window, and tend to be attached to a specific item that resides in it. This might be a single element, a set of elements, the HTML document loaded in the current tab, or the entire browser window.
There are many different types of events that can occur.
For example:
The user selects, clicks, or hovers the cursor over a certain element.
The user presses a key on the keyboard.
The user resizes or closes the browser window.
A web page finishes loading.
A form is submitted.
A video is played, paused, or ends.
An error occurs.
You can gather from this (and from glancing at the
event index
) that there are
a lot
of events that can be fired.
To react to an event, you attach an
event listener
to it. This is a code feature that listens out for the event firing. When the event fires, an
event handler
function (referenced by, or contained inside the event listener) is called to respond to the event firing. When such a block of code is set up to run in response to an event, we say we are
registering an event handler
.
An example: handling a click event
In the following example, we have a single
<button>
in the page:
html
<button>Change color</button>
button {
margin: 10px;
}
Then we have some JavaScript. We'll look at this in more detail in the next section, but for now we can just say: it adds an event listener to the button's
"click"
event, and the contained handler function reacts to the event by setting the page background to a random color:
js
const btn = document.querySelector("button");
function random(number) {
return Math.floor(Math.random() * (number + 1));
}
btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
const rndCol = `rgb(${random(255)} ${random(255)} ${random(255)})`;
document.body.style.backgroundColor = rndCol;
});
The example output is as follows. Try clicking the button:
Using addEventListener()
As we saw in the last example, objects that can fire events have an
addEventListener()
method, and this is the recommended mechanism for adding event listeners.
Let's take a closer look at the code from the last example:
js
const btn = document.querySelector("button");
function random(number) {
return Math.floor(Math.random() * (number + 1));
}
btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
const rndCol = `rgb(${random(255)} ${random(255)} ${random(255)})`;
document.body.style.backgroundColor = rndCol;
});
The HTML
<button>
element will fire a
click
event when the user clicks it. We call the
addEventListener()
method on it to add an event listener; this takes two parameters:
the string
"click"
, to indicate that we want to listen to the
click
event. Buttons can fire lots of other events, such as
"mouseover"
when the user moves their mouse over the button, or
"keydown"
when the user presses a key and the button is focused.
a function to call when the event happens. In our case, the defined anonymous function generates a random RGB color and sets the
background-color
of the page
<body>
to that color.
You could also create a separate named function, and reference that in the second parameter of
addEventListener()
, like this:
js
const btn = document.querySelector("button");
function random(number) {
return Math.floor(Math.random() * (number + 1));
}
function changeBackground() {
const rndCol = `rgb(${random(255)} ${random(255)} ${random(255)})`;
document.body.style.backgroundColor = rndCol;
}
btn.addEventListener("click", changeBackground);
Listening for other events
There are many different events that can be fired by a button element. Let's experiment.
First, make a local copy of
random-color-addeventlistener.html
, and open it in your browser.
It's just a copy of the simple random color example we've played with already. Now try changing
click
to the following different values in turn, and observi

data.title: Creating the Longest Possible Ski Jump in “The Games: Winter Challenge”
data.author: alberto-m
data.article_summary: 本文主要讲述了作者对经典游戏《The Games: Winter Challenge》中跳台滑雪项目的研究，目标是创造最优跳跃距离。起初，作者被游戏的复制保护机制分散了注意力，后来发现该机制限制了跳跃距离。去除保护后，作者成功跳出了超过100米的距离。作者提出了两种方法来探索跳跃距离的极限：一是使用工具辅助的逐帧输入测试，二是通过分析游戏二进制代码深入理解其物理模拟机制。作者选择后者，计划通过分析游戏代码重现跳跃逻辑，并生成最佳输入序列以实现最优跳跃。文章还介绍了游戏中跳台滑雪的四个阶段，并指出游戏手册建议的技巧可能并非最优，开发者意图和实际最佳策略可能不同。作者希望通过技术分析找到隐藏的机制，实现超越常规的跳跃成绩。

44825347.article_content:
After spending way too much time getting side-tracked with
investigating the copy protection measures
, it is time to return to the actual reason I started looking into The Games: Winter Challenge to begin with: The quest to create the optimal ski jump and see how far you can push the game.
One of my initial questions was already answered, namely whether it’s possible to jump farther than 100 meters, a feat that I never managed as a kid.
One of the hidden copy protection measures of the game limits how far you can jump when they are active, and without them I jumped farther without too much trouble:
I’d like to think that I’m just better at video games than I was as a kid, but realistically I likely could have achieved this decades ago without the artificial limitations the copy protection adds.
But the big question of “how far can you go?” still remained.
I see two possible avenues for going about answering it.
One is to build some form of harness to allow individually controlling the inputs the game receives, advancing one frame at a time and using savestates to try many different input sequences to see which produces the best result.
This is how most
tool-assisted speedruns
for video games are created, using special emulators which have those functions built-in.
However, this method has some drawbacks. For one, it is limited by your understanding of and creativity within the game: if there is some hidden mechanic you don’t know about, you won’t be able to exploit it.
Also, if there are too many different possibilities to try, it can be very tedious to try them by hand, and doing it programmatically can be fairly slow because you need to emulate the whole game millions of times.
Instead, I will be going for a more analytical approach.
We will not be playing the game at all, and instead crack the game binary open and deeply understand how it functions.
By learning all the details of how the game runs the simulation, we can analyze how it represents the game state, how it runs its physics simulation, and how it determines the actual distance traveled.
Maybe by this we will learn that the answer is as simple as “keep as straight as possible to maximize distance”.
Likely the logic will be much more complicated than that though, and it should be possible to create a model re-implementation of the ski jump logic, extracting only the relevant parts and run much more efficient simulations on it.
Then, by learning how the game’s replay file format works, we can create our own synthetic replays using the input sequences we found from our simulations, and play them back in the game, achieving the optimal ski jump entirely outside the game itself.
The basic mechanics of the ski jump event
To start off, let’s go over how a ski jump in the game works in general.
There are four main phases for each jump:
First, you go down the jumping ramp and can move the jumper left and right, counteracting random winds pushing you around.
Then, you jump off the take-off table, by pressing down at the right time, which determines how high your jumper will lift off.
Next, you fly over the hill, and can press up and down in order to adjust the angle of the skis for a more aerodynamic position, again with some wind randomly pushing against you.
Finally, you press Enter as you approach the ground to land safely.
The game itself, as well as its manual, give some hints as to how you’re supposed to use your controls in order to jump farther.
While going down the ramp, if you stray too far left or right, the game renders puffs of snow and plays a corresponding sound, indicating to you that you’re going off the track and are slowing down.
During the flight section, while the game itself doesn’t give you any direct feedback on whether what you’re doing is good, the game’s manual recommends keeping the skis parallel during the flight to minimize drag.
This “parallel style” is a great reminder of the game’s age, as it was in fact the dominant
ski jump technique
up until the early 90’s when this game was created, and was since replaced by the now dominant “V-style” of forming a V-shape with the skis.
The game does allow you to form a V-shape as well, but it’s unlikely that it simulates air resistance in any meaningful way, and I assume that what is optimal is what the developers wanted you to do, instead of what is actually better in the real world.
Overall, this surface-level analysis goes by what the game itself tells us is good or bad, but there is no guarantee that this is actually true.
For one, there could be hidden mechanics that influence the jump which are not explained directly.
And even if that isn’t the case, what the developers intended to be the optimal strategy, and what the optimal strategy actually is, can be very different things.
It’s quite plausible that there are some emergent behaviors that the developers didn’t anticipate, but which can help us achieve better results.

data.title: PHP compile time generics: yay or nay?
data.author: moebrowne
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了在PHP中实现编译时泛型的可能性和优缺点。泛型是一种允许类型作为参数传递的特性，常见于编译型语言，但在解释型语言如PHP中实现非常困难。PHP基金会开发团队的实验表明，可能只需付出20%的努力就能获得80%的收益。他们建议仅在接口和抽象类上实现泛型，从而避免大部分潜在问题。

具体做法是让接口和抽象类声明需要指定的类型，例如`interface Exporter<Thing>`，而实现这些接口的类则需填充具体类型，如`class WidgetExporter implements Exporter<Widget>`。所有类型替换在编译时完成，这使得类型检查更快，并在编译时捕获大多数错误。

尽管运行时泛型仍无法实现，但部分实现并不会使问题变得更复杂。文章还提到“关联类型”的概念，它类似于泛型，可以在编译时解决特定问题。实验表明，这种部分实现的泛型能提供大部分预期的好处。

Compile time generics: yay or nay?
Published on
Aug 04, 2025
by
Larry Garfield
,
Gina Banyard
Stories
One of the most sought-after features for PHP is Generics: The ability to have a type that takes another type as a parameter.  It's a feature found in most compiled languages by now, but implementing generics in an interpreted language like PHP, where all the type checking would have to be done at runtime, has always proven Really Really Hard(tm), Really Really Slow(tm), or both.
But, experimentation by the PHP Foundation's dev team suggests we may be able to get 80% of the benefit for 20% of the work.  Is that enough?
The short, short version
We believe it's possible to implement generics on only interfaces and abstract classes, which would offer a large chunk of the benefit of generics but avoid most of the pitfalls.
In particular, interfaces and abstract classes could declare that they need one or more types specified:
interface Exporter<Thing> { ... }
And then classes that implement/extend them would be required to fill in those types:
class WidgetExporter implements Exporter<Widget> { ... }
And then anywhere the type
Thing
appeared in
Exporter
, it would turn into
Widget
in
WidgetExporter
.
All of this is done at compile time, which makes it far easier and faster, and many/most errors would be caught at compile time.
Runtime generics, where you could say
$fooExporter = new Exporter<Foo>()
, would still not be possible, but they do not get any harder as a result of going just part way.
Would you support (and vote in favor of) compile-time-only generics as described below?
Prior research
In 2023 and 2024, Arnaud Le Blanc from the Foundation team did
extensive experimentation
on generics, picking up on the previous work from Nikita Popov.  The full result of that experiment is available at that link, but in short, some parts of generics would be possible, even straightforward.  Where the edge cases run into problems, though, they are very big problems.
In particular:
Union types and generics combine to produce massive performance penalties.
Many cases would result in a very cumbersome syntax unless we had really good type inference.
Really good type inference is hard and slow, especially in PHP.
Meanwhile, making arrays generic, and therefore typed, had its own challenges, especially given that PHP variables are not typed.
Arnaud and Larry Garfield did further investigation afterward into introducing
a "module" system
that would help PHP's compiler
see more code at once
, and thus be able to do type inference more readily, but sadly that also ran into many challenging edge cases.
Associated Types
In mid-2025, the Foundation's Gina Banyard started working on "associated types," a generics-adjacent feature found in a few languages that happens entirely at compile time. It essentially allows a class or interface to specify that inheritors must specify a type to be used in certain situations.  Initially, it was intended as an alternative to the
never
parameters
RFC, offering a better solution to the case of an interface that doesn't need to specify a particular type, but implementing classes do.
The initial plan looked something like this:
interface ImporterExporter
{
type T;
public function import(string $input): T;
public function export(T $value): string;
}
class ThingImporter implements ImporterExporter
{
public function import(string $input): Thing { ... }
public function export(Thing $value): string { ... }
}
In which all references to
T
in the interface need to be replaced by the
same
type in the class; it can be any type, as long as it's the same in all cases.
After some discussion with the rest of the team, however, it became apparent that if we just changed the spelling and squinted, associated types look an awful lot like generics.  Or rather, part of generics, as full generics is a very involved bit of functionality with lots of different complimentary parts.
Which begged the question: Could we just do some of those parts, and get most of the benefit?  According to Gina's work, the answer is "Probably!"
Abstract Generics
What Gina has implemented, though it still needs some polish and extension, is essentially "manually monomorphized generics," implemented at compile time.  "Monomorphization" is an approach to generics (there are others) where a type-specific version of a class is created "on the fly" by the compiler or engine when that type-specific version is used.  By "manual," we mean that it's up to the developer to do so in advance.
Let's see what that looks like in practice.
Consider our previous interface, but spelled this way instead:
interface ImporterExporter<T>
{
public function import(string $input): T;
public function export(T $value): string;
}
That interface requires that any class implementing it specify what type
T
should be; it can be any type, as long as it's the same type in both places.
class ThingExporter implements ImporterExporter<Thing>
{

• Waterluvian：观察到有些人花费大量时间设置工作环境以提高生产力，但实际生产力并未显著提升。他们更多关注于“准备工作”的 meta 层面，而非实际执行任务。

• magicmicah85：赞赏该设备的理念，但认为自己的生产力问题源于心理而非设备，因此不认为新设备能解决问题，反而可能增加不必要的复杂性。

• cosmic_cheese：建议扩展设备尺寸以容纳全键盘，使其更适合写作任务，并提到现有的e-ink平板在键盘连接和系统流畅性上的不足。
• WorldPeas：质疑为何许多标榜“生产力”的设备并未真正提升生产力，认为市场宣传与其功能不符。
• protocolture：希望有一种价格低于50美元、具备键盘和WiFi功能的设备。
• ZiiS：关注设备的价格，认为若价格过高可能影响购买意愿，并提到复杂手表可以从中国以低价购得，暗示对该PDA成本的比较。
• qwerty456127：认为设备按键数量太少，影响使用。
• RajT88：表达对该设备的兴趣，同时怀念过去多样化的移动设备市场，认为当前市场过于单一，主要由iPhone主导。
• righthand：担心该项目在美国关税政策下可能面临的生存问题。

• 关于设备价格的讨论，部分用户关注其性价比及生产成本。
• 对EPD显示屏的技术讨论，指出其在编程复杂性和用户体验上的潜在问题。
• 对键盘设计的不同看法，有的用户强调全键盘的重要性，有的则关注按键数量和布局。

• 生产力设备的实际效果：部分用户质疑这些设备是否真正提升了生产力，还是仅仅停留在准备工作的层面。
• 设备的设计和功能取舍：例如键盘的实用性、显示屏的技术选择等，用户在这些具体设计上存在不同偏好和意见。
• 设备价格与其功能和性价比之间的关系，部分用户认为高价设备应具备更多功能，但也有人希望设备保持简单并降低成本。

data.title: The great myth of empire collapse
data.author: marojejian
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了古代帝国崩溃对普通人的实际影响，以阿卡德帝国和乌尔第三王朝为例。尽管文学作品如《阿卡德诅咒》描绘了城市的毁灭和自然灾害，但考古证据显示，阿卡德城在王朝更替后仍有人居住，普通人生活如常。作者指出，传统历史叙述往往聚焦于帝国的辉煌与衰落，但通过研究普通人的健康状况，如骨骸和牙齿的分析，可以发现帝国崩溃未必直接导致生活质量下降。文章强调，这种视角有助于更全面地理解历史，并为当今社会提供借鉴。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：帝国崩溃对日常生活的影响

不同观点：
• Muromec认为，除了宏观视角外，普通人在帝国和帝国崩溃时的日常生活体验也非常重要。他以1990年代频繁停电和缺水为例，说明即使生活质量在之后的一二十年有所改善，但当时的困难对生活造成了负面影响。

• Charcircuit的观点则是，帝国崩溃的影响可以通过询问经历过这种崩溃的人来理解。他以英国帝国在过去100年内的崩溃为例，认为仍然可以找到生活在其中的人，询问他们的亲身经历。

补充讨论：
• Muromec强调了帝国崩溃对普通人日常生活的直接影响，特别是基础设施和服务的中断，如停电和缺水。
• Charcircuit则侧重于通过当代人的口述历史来理解帝国崩溃的影响，认为可以通过这些亲历者的描述获取对崩溃过程的直接认识。
• 争议的焦点在于理解帝国崩溃影响的最佳方式：是通过分析日常生活中的具体困难（Muromec的观点），还是通过收集经历过崩溃的人的直接证言（charcircuit的观点）。

44857882.article_content:
No one walks among the wild goats and darting snakes of the mountain, its steppe where grew the succulent plants grew nothing but the reed of tears … Akkad is destroyed!
This lament is from the ‘Curse of Akkad’, a poem written about the fall of the Akkadian Empire, which reigned more than
4,000 years
ago in the Near East. Yet it’s more myth than reality: despite the tragic language about a destroyed city, the capital of Akkad did not disappear. It was still occupied and, later, new kings took over its rule: the Third Dynasty of Ur. That empire fell too, eventually, and is also remembered through literature written years after its demise: ‘The malicious storm which swept over the Land, the storm which destroyed cities, the storm which destroyed houses … the storm which cut off all that is good from the Land.’ This natural disaster was apparently caused by Enlil, the god of the winds. Yet there’s no archaeological evidence for this.
Imprint made from a cylinder seal from the Third Dynasty of Ur, possibly depicting king Ur-Nammu (right). Courtesy the
British Museum, London
In fact, as far as we can tell, life continued normally for citizens of Akkad and Ur. As the archaeologist Guy Middleton points out in
Understanding Collapse
(2017), the empires may have died, but the average person might not have even noticed.
Until recently, many archaeologists focused on revealing the cultural glories and dynastic power of such civilisations. The Akkadians left us
cuneiform
records (writing inscribed with reeds onto clay) and staggering ziggurats (massive, terraced, flat-topped temples). And Ur-Namma, the first king of the Third Dynasty of Ur, left us the earliest known legal code. This means that popular perceptions of many past empires, such as Rome or the Qin, focus on their great artwork and monumental achievements, such as the
Colosseum
or the Great Wall of China.
In recent years, many archaeologists and historians have taken a different approach, asking: what was it like as an ordinary person to live through these imperial collapses? You may assume that a collapse in the imperial superstructure meant that people went hungry and homeless, and that is certainly the picture in the poems of lamentation and sorrow. But the physical evidence of people’s health, for instance, shows something very different.
As a researcher who studies the causes of civilisation collapse to inform policy in the present, I believe this matters. In textbooks, museums and popular culture, history is often told as a tale of rise and fall. It is a story of human progress during the reign of empires and kingdoms, followed by regression and barbarism when these fade away. This is why we have the idea of imperial ‘
golden ages
’ of wealth, peace and cultural advances, followed by a descent into ‘dark ages’ marked by violence, poverty and stagnation. Yet this is history through the eyes of elites. Not only does this skew our understanding of the past, but it also shapes how we think about collapse in the present and future.
M
any of us know of the brutality of life under empire, although we perhaps underestimate just how bad it could be. Armed men rounding up women to sell them into slavery or public crucifixions are today seen with dismay when done by the Islamic State in Syria and Iraq but, as the historian Walter Scheidel
observed
, these were a normal sight in Rome during its peak. Rome was also a pyramid scheme that was at war more than
90 pe
r cent of the time between 410 and
101 BCE.
In China, the Shang Dynasty
sacrificed
around 13,000 people over two centuries, and the Qin dynasty killed an
estimated
1.5 million
people to establish unified rule.
Yet, those who judge human progress only by technological advances and economic growth might believe these grim realities were for the greater good. Empires, in the typical telling, may have been harsh in their punishments and brutal towards their enemies, but also pacified their citizens, ensured security, and hence enabled far greater economic and social prosperity.
But did those citizens actually prosper under empire, and suffer when it vanished?
To answer that question we need to assess the wellbeing of populations thousands of years ago. This is tricky. Medical records are usually absent, and written documents are subjective, but we can get clues from the physical health of people’s bodies. For example, an approach called ‘osteoarcheology’ examines the bones of past people. Bones with fewer lesions (damage from trauma and infections) tend to suggest stronger skeletons, and less exposure to disease and violence. Teeth with fewer holes (caries) tend to suggest a better, less-carbohydrate rich diet. Most importantly, taller people usually mean healthier people, with better diets and less trauma from famine and disease.
Pharaohs and their wives were taller than men and women in the general ancient Egyptian population

data.author: HR01
data.article_summary: 文章简要介绍了科幻作品中的“牵引光束”概念，其最早由E.E. "Doc" Smith在1931年提出，并在《星际迷航》和《星球大战》等作品中广泛使用。尽管在科幻中这是常见的虚构技术，但现实中科学家们已通过光波和声波实现了小规模的牵引光束，能移动微小物体。这些技术利用声场或光场形成力场，困住并移动目标。目前，声波牵引光束已能移动如泡沫球等小物体，而光波牵引光束则限于微观粒子，因激光加热问题难以扩大规模。未来，这种技术有望在医疗或工业中得到实际应用。
